sentences.zh: 李維楨，字本寧，京山人。

translations.literal: Li Weizhen, whose courtesy name was Benning, was a native of Jingshan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Weizhen, styled Benning, came from Jingshan.

sentences.zh: 父裕，福建布政使。

translations.literal: His father Yu served as Administrative Commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu had served as provincial commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 維楨舉隆慶二年進士，由庶吉士授編修。

translations.literal: Weizhen passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Longqing and, after serving as a Hanlin bachelor, was appointed Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhen earned his jinshi degree in the second year of Longqing and, following a stint as a Hanlin bachelor, was made a compiler.

sentences.zh: 萬歷時，《穆宗實錄》成，進修撰。

translations.literal: During the Wanli reign, when the 《Veritable Records of Emperor Muzong》 were completed, he was promoted to Sub-Editor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wanli reign, after the 《Veritable Records of Emperor Muzong》 were finished, he was promoted to sub-editor.

sentences.zh: 出為陜西右參議，遷提學副使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Right Assistant Administrator of Shaanxi and later transferred to Vice Commissioner of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital to serve as right assistant administrator of Shaanxi, then was transferred to vice commissioner of education.

sentences.zh: 浮沈外僚，幾三十年。

translations.literal: He drifted among provincial posts for nearly thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: He remained in provincial service, rising and falling without advancement, for nearly thirty years.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，以布政使家居，年七十余矣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tianqi reign, he was living at home as a provincial commissioner and was already over seventy.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianqi reign he was retired at home, having served as a provincial commissioner, and was already over seventy.

sentences.zh: 會朝議登用耆舊，召為南京太仆卿，旋改太常，未赴。

translations.literal: When the court discussed appointing venerable officials, he was summoned as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud at Nanjing, then transferred to Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, but he did not take up either post.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated recalling elderly worthies to office, he was summoned as vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud at Nanjing and soon after reassigned to vice minister of imperial sacrifices, but he never reported.

sentences.zh: 聞諫官有言，辭不就。

translations.literal: When he heard that remonstrance officials had spoken against it, he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that censorial officials had objected, he declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 時方修《神宗實錄》，給事中薛大中特疏薦之，未及用。

translations.literal: At the time the 《Veritable Records of Emperor Shenzong》 were being compiled, Censor-in-Chief Xue Dazhong especially memorialized recommending him, but the appointment was not made in time.
translations.idiomatic: While the 《Veritable Records of Emperor Shenzong》 were being compiled, Censor-in-Chief Xue Dazhong submitted a special memorial recommending him, but the appointment did not come through in time.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，太常卿董其昌復薦之，乃召為禮部右侍郎，甫三月進尚書，並在南京。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year, Dong Qichang, Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, again recommended him; he was then summoned as Vice Minister of Rites, and after only three months was promoted to Minister—all at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year, Minister of Imperial Sacrifices Dong Qichang recommended him again; he was summoned as vice minister of rites and, only three months later, promoted to minister—both posts at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 維楨緣史事起用，乃館中諸臣憚其以前輩壓己，不令入館，但超遷其官。

translations.literal: Weizhen had been recalled on account of the history project, but the officials in the Hanlin Academy feared him as a senior who would overshadow them and did not allow him to enter the Academy, merely elevating his rank in a special promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhen had been recalled for work on the history, but the academicians feared him as a senior who would overshadow them and kept him out of the Hanlin Academy, granting him only an extraordinary promotion in rank.

sentences.zh: 維楨亦以年衰，明年正月力乞骸骨去。

translations.literal: Weizhen, considering his advanced age, the following year in the first month forcefully petitioned to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhen, feeling the weight of his years, the next year in the first month petitioned forcefully to retire.

sentences.zh: 又明年卒於家，年八十。

translations.literal: The year after that he died at home, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that he died at home, at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: During the Chongzhen reign he was posthumously granted the title of Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongzhen reign he was posthumously ennobled as grand guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 維楨弱冠登朝，博聞強記，與同館許國齊名。

translations.literal: Weizhen entered court service in his early twenties; widely learned with a powerful memory, he was as renowned as his fellow Hanlin member Xu Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhen entered court service before he was twenty; widely read with an exceptional memory, he was as famous as his fellow academician Xu Guo.

sentences.zh: 館中為之語曰：「記不得，問老許；

translations.literal: A saying circulated in the Academy: "If you cannot remember, ask old Xu;
translations.idiomatic: A saying went around the Academy: "If you cannot remember, ask old Xu;

sentences.zh: 做不得，問小李。」

translations.literal: if you cannot manage it, ask young Li.
translations.idiomatic: if you cannot manage it, ask young Li.

sentences.zh: 維楨為人，樂易闊達，賓客雜進。

translations.literal: Weizhen's character was open, easygoing, and broad-minded; guests of all sorts came and went.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhen was by nature open, easygoing, and broad-minded, and guests of every sort came and went.

sentences.zh: 其文章，弘肆有才氣，海內請求者無虛日，能屈曲以副其所望。

translations.literal: His writings were expansive and spirited; petitions from across the realm arrived daily without fail, and he could bend his style to satisfy whatever was requested.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was expansive and spirited; requests from across the realm arrived daily without fail, and he could shape his writing to meet whatever was asked of him.

sentences.zh: 碑版之文，照耀四裔。

translations.literal: His commemorative inscriptions shone across the four quarters of the world.
translations.idiomatic: His commemorative inscriptions were celebrated in every corner of the realm.

sentences.zh: 門下士招富人大賈，受取金錢，代為請乞，亦應之無倦，負重名垂四十年。

translations.literal: His disciples solicited wealthy merchants; accepting payment, they begged him to compose on their behalf, and he answered without weariness, bearing a great reputation for nearly forty years.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples brought in wealthy merchants, took their money, and begged him to write on their behalf; he answered without weariness and carried a great name for nearly forty years.

sentences.zh: 然文多率意應酬，品格不能高也。

translations.literal: Yet most of his writings were casual responses to requests, and their quality could not be high.
translations.idiomatic: Yet most of his writing was casual work done to oblige others, and its quality could not be high.

sentences.zh: 邑人郝敬，字仲輿。

translations.literal: A fellow townsman, Hao Jing, whose courtesy name was Zhongyu.
translations.idiomatic: A fellow townsman, Hao Jing, styled Zhongyu.

sentences.zh: 父承健，舉於鄉，官肅寧知縣。

translations.literal: His father Chengjian passed the provincial examination and served as magistrate of Suning.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chengjian passed the provincial examination and served as magistrate of Suning.

sentences.zh: 敬幼稱神童，性跅弛，嘗殺人系獄。

translations.literal: Jing was called a child prodigy in youth; his nature was unrestrained, and he once killed someone and was imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Jing was hailed as a prodigy, but his nature was undisciplined; he once killed a man and was imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 維楨，其父執也，援出之，館於家。

translations.literal: Weizhen, who was his father's close friend, secured his release and kept him as a guest in his home.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhen, a close friend of his father, secured his release and took him in as a guest.

sentences.zh: 始折節讀書，舉萬歷十七年進士。

translations.literal: Only then did Jing rein himself in to study, and he passed the jinshi examination in the seventeenth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Jing apply himself to his studies, and he passed the jinshi examination in the seventeenth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 歷知縉雲、永嘉二縣，並有能聲。

translations.literal: He served successively as magistrate of Jinyun and Yongjia, earning a reputation for competence at both.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as magistrate of Jinyun and Yongjia, winning a reputation for competence at both posts.

sentences.zh: 征授禮科給事中，乞假歸養。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Censor-in-Chief in the Office of Rites, then requested leave to return home and care for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed censor-in-chief in the Office of Rites, then requested leave to return home and care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 久之，補戶科，數有所論奏。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was transferred to the Office of Revenue, where he submitted several memorials.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was transferred to the Office of Revenue, where he submitted several memorials.

sentences.zh: 山東稅監陳增貪橫，為益都知縣吳宗堯所奏，帝不罪。

translations.literal: The tax supervisor of Shandong, Chen Zeng, was greedy and overbearing; he was impeached by Wu Zongyao, magistrate of Yidu, but the emperor did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zeng, the tax supervisor in Shandong, was greedy and overbearing; Wu Zongyao, magistrate of Yidu, impeached him, but the emperor did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 敬上言：「開采不罷，則陛下明旨不過為愚弄臣民之虛文。

translations.literal: Jing memorialized: "If mining is not halted, Your Majesty's clear edict will be nothing but empty words to deceive officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: Jing memorialized: "If mining is not halted, Your Majesty's clear edict will be nothing but empty words meant to deceive officials and people.

sentences.zh: 乞先停止，然後以宗堯所奏下撫按勘核，正增不法之罪。」

translations.literal: I beg that it be stopped first; then let the memorial submitted by Zongyao be sent down to the governor and inspector for investigation, and Chen Zeng's unlawful crimes be properly punished.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that it be stopped first; then let Zongyao's memorial be sent down to the governor and inspector for investigation, so that Zeng's unlawful crimes may be properly punished.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not agree.

sentences.zh: 頃之，山東巡撫尹應元亦極論增罪，帝怒，切責應元，斥完堯為民。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, Grand Coordinator Yin Yingyuan of Shandong also strongly denounced Zeng's crimes; the emperor was angry, sharply rebuked Yingyuan, and demoted Zongyao to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, Grand Coordinator Yin Yingyuan of Shandong also strongly denounced Zeng's crimes; the emperor was furious, sharply rebuked Yingyuan, and demoted Zongyao to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 敬再上言：「陛下處陳增一事，甚失眾心。」

translations.literal: Jing memorialized again: "Your Majesty's handling of the Chen Zeng affair has greatly lost the hearts of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Jing memorialized again: "Your Majesty's handling of the Chen Zeng affair has greatly lost the hearts of the people.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，奪俸一年。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and stripped him of salary for one year.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and stripped him of salary for one year.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中官高寀榷稅京口，暨祿榷稅儀真，敬復力諫。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched the eunuch Gao Cai to levy taxes at Jingkou and Ji Lu to levy taxes at Yizhen; Jing again remonstrated forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched the eunuch Gao Cai to levy taxes at Jingkou and Ji Lu to levy taxes at Yizhen; Jing remonstrated forcefully again.

sentences.zh: 宗堯之劾增也，增怒甚，誣訐其贓私，詞連青州一府官僚，旁引商民吳時奉等，請皆籍沒，帝輒可之。

translations.literal: When Zongyao impeached Zeng, Zeng was furious and falsely accused him of corruption, implicating the entire bureaucracy of Qingzhou prefecture and citing in addition the merchant Wu Shifeng and others, requesting that all their property be confiscated; the emperor promptly approved.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongyao impeached Zeng, Zeng was furious and falsely accused him of corruption, implicating the entire bureaucracy of Qingzhou prefecture and naming in addition the merchant Wu Shifeng and others, requesting that all their property be confiscated; the emperor promptly approved.

sentences.zh: 敬復力詆增，乞速寢其奏，亦不納。

translations.literal: Jing again fiercely denounced Zeng and begged that the memorial be quickly withdrawn, but this too was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Jing again fiercely denounced Zeng and begged that the memorial be quickly withdrawn, but this too was rejected.

sentences.zh: 坐事，謫知江陰縣。

translations.literal: For an offense he was demoted to magistrate of Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense he was demoted to magistrate of Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 貪汙不檢，物論皆不予，遂投劾歸，杜門著書。

translations.literal: Corrupt and undisciplined, public opinion universally condemned him; he then submitted his resignation and returned home, closing his doors to write books.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt and undisciplined, he won no public esteem; he then submitted his resignation, returned home, and shut his doors to write books.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the twelfth year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 徐渭，字文長，山陰人。

translations.literal: Xu Wei, whose courtesy name was Wenchang, was a native of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wei, styled Wenchang, came from Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 十余歲仿揚雄《解嘲》作《釋毀》，長師同里季本。

translations.literal: At over ten years of age he composed the 《Explaining Slander》, modeled on Yang Xiong's 《Defending Ridicule》; in youth he studied under Ji Ben of the same district.
translations.idiomatic: Before he was fully grown he composed the 《Explaining Slander》, modeled on Yang Xiong's 《Defending Ridicule》, and in youth studied under Ji Ben of the same district.

sentences.zh: 為諸生，有盛名。

translations.literal: As a licentiate he possessed great renown.
translations.idiomatic: As a licentiate he enjoyed great renown.

sentences.zh: 總督胡宗憲招致幕府，與歙余寅、鄞沈明臣同憲書記。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Hu Zongxian invited him into his staff, where he served as Hu's secretary alongside Yu Yin of She and Shen Mingchen of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Hu Zongxian brought him into his staff, where he served as Hu's secretary alongside Yu Yin of She and Shen Mingchen of Yin.

sentences.zh: 宗憲得白鹿，將獻諸朝，令渭草表，並他客草寄所善學士，擇其尤上之。

translations.literal: Zongxian obtained a white deer and intended to present it to the court; he had Wei draft a memorial and also sent drafts by other guests to a scholar he favored, selecting the best one to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Zongxian obtained a white deer and intended to present it at court; he had Wei draft a memorial and also sent drafts by other guests to a scholar he favored, choosing the best one to submit.

sentences.zh: 學士以渭表進，世宗大悅，益寵異宗憲，宗憲以是益重渭。

translations.literal: The scholar submitted Wei's memorial; Emperor Shizong was greatly pleased, bestowed even greater favor on Zongxian, and Zongxian therefore valued Wei all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The scholar submitted Wei's memorial; Emperor Shizong was greatly pleased, bestowed even greater favor on Zongxian, and Zongxian therefore valued Wei all the more.

sentences.zh: 宗憲嘗宴將吏於爛柯山，酒酣樂作，明臣作《鐃歌》十章，中有雲「狹巷短兵相接處，殺人如草不聞聲」。

translations.literal: Zongxian once feasted his officers at Mount Lanke; when the wine was warm and music playing, Mingchen composed ten 《Naoge》 songs, one of which ran, 「In the narrow lanes where short weapons meet, men are cut down like grass without a sound.」
translations.idiomatic: Zongxian once feasted his officers at Mount Lanke; when the wine was warm and music was playing, Mingchen composed ten 《Naoge》 songs, one of which ran, 「In the narrow lanes where short weapons meet, men are cut down like grass without a sound.」

sentences.zh: 宗憲起，捋其須曰：「何物沈生，雄快乃爾！」

translations.literal: Zongxian rose, stroked his beard, and said: "What sort of fellow is this Master Shen—so bold and spirited!
translations.idiomatic: Zongxian rose, stroked his beard, and said: "What sort of fellow is this Master Shen—so bold and spirited!

sentences.zh: 即命刻於石，寵禮與渭埒。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered it carved in stone and favored him with honors equal to Wei's.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered it carved in stone and honored him with favors equal to Wei's.

sentences.zh: 督府勢嚴重，將吏莫敢仰視。

translations.literal: The governor's headquarters was awesome in authority; officers and clerks did not dare look up.
translations.idiomatic: The governor's headquarters was formidable in authority; officers and clerks did not dare look up.

sentences.zh: 渭角巾布衣，長揖縱談。

translations.literal: Wei wore a kerchief and plain robes, bowed with hands clasped, and spoke freely.
translations.idiomatic: Wei wore a kerchief and plain robes, bowed with hands clasped, and spoke freely.

sentences.zh: 幕中有急需，夜深開戟門以待。

translations.literal: When the staff had urgent business, at deep night they would open the halberd gate to await him.
translations.idiomatic: When the staff had urgent business, they would open the halberd gate deep into the night to await him.

sentences.zh: 渭或醉不至，宗憲顧善之。

translations.literal: Wei might be drunk and fail to come; Zongxian nevertheless looked upon it favorably.
translations.idiomatic: Wei might be drunk and fail to come; Zongxian nevertheless looked upon it favorably.

sentences.zh: 寅、明臣亦頗負崖岸，以侃直見禮。

translations.literal: Yin and Mingchen likewise bore themselves with lofty dignity and were honored for their frank straightforwardness.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and Mingchen likewise carried themselves with lofty dignity and were honored for their frank straightforwardness.

sentences.zh: 渭知兵，好奇計，宗憲擒徐海，誘王直，皆預其謀。

translations.literal: Wei understood warfare and delighted in daring stratagems; in Zongxian's capture of Xu Hai and enticement of Wang Zhi, he participated in the planning of both.
translations.idiomatic: Wei understood warfare and delighted in daring stratagems; he took part in planning both Zongxian's capture of Xu Hai and his enticement of Wang Zhi.

sentences.zh: 藉宗憲勢，頗橫。

translations.literal: Relying on Zongxian's power, he became somewhat overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Relying on Zongxian's power, he became somewhat overbearing.

sentences.zh: 及宗憲下獄，渭懼禍，遂發狂，引巨錐剚耳，深數寸，又以椎碎腎囊，皆不死。

translations.literal: When Zongxian was imprisoned, Wei feared disaster and went mad; he drove a large awl into his ear several inches deep and smashed his scrotum with a mallet, yet did not die.
translations.idiomatic: When Zongxian was imprisoned, Wei feared disaster and went mad; he drove a large awl into his ear several inches deep and smashed his scrotum with a mallet, yet did not die.

sentences.zh: 已，又擊殺繼妻，論死系獄，裏人張元忭力救得免。

translations.literal: Later he struck and killed his stepwife, was sentenced to death and imprisoned; his fellow townsman Zhang Yuanbian fought hard to save him and secured his release.
translations.idiomatic: Later he struck and killed his stepwife, was sentenced to death and imprisoned; his fellow townsman Zhang Yuanbian fought hard to save him and secured his release.

sentences.zh: 乃遊金陵，抵宣、遼，縱觀諸邊厄塞，善李成梁諸子。

translations.literal: He then traveled to Jinling, reaching Xuancheng and Liaodong, roamed the strategic passes along the frontiers, and befriended the sons of Li Chengliang.
translations.idiomatic: He then traveled to Jinling, reaching Xuancheng and Liaodong, roamed the strategic passes along the frontiers, and befriended the sons of Li Chengliang.

sentences.zh: 入京師，主元忭。

translations.literal: Entering the capital, he lodged with Yuanbian.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the capital, he lodged with Yuanbian.

sentences.zh: 元忭導以禮法，渭不能從，久之怒而去。

translations.literal: Yuanbian guided him with ritual and propriety, but Wei could not follow; after a long while he left in anger.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbian guided him with ritual and propriety, but Wei could not follow; after a long while he left in anger.

sentences.zh: 後元忭卒，白衣往吊，撫棺慟哭，不告姓名去。

translations.literal: Later, when Yuanbian died, Wei went in white mourning clothes to offer condolences, stroked the coffin and wept bitterly, then left without giving his name.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Yuanbian died, Wei went in white mourning clothes to offer condolences, stroked the coffin and wept bitterly, then left without giving his name.

sentences.zh: 渭天才超軼，詩文絕出倫輩。

translations.literal: Wei had talent surpassing the extraordinary, and his poetry and prose were utterly beyond his peers.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wei possessed talent that surpassed the ordinary, and his poetry and prose stood utterly above his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 善草書，工寫花草竹石。

translations.literal: He was skilled at cursive script and adept at painting flowers, grasses, bamboo, and rocks.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at cursive calligraphy and was adept at painting flowers, grasses, bamboo, and rocks.

sentences.zh: 嘗自言：「吾書第一，詩次之，文次之，畫又次之。」

translations.literal: He once said of himself: 「My calligraphy is first, poetry second, prose third, and painting again last.
translations.idiomatic: He once said of himself: "My calligraphy comes first, poetry second, prose third, and painting last of all.

sentences.zh: 當嘉靖時，王、李倡七子社，謝榛以布衣被擯。

translations.literal: During the Jiajing period, Wang and Li founded the Seven Masters society, and Xie Zhen, as a commoner in plain cloth, was cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jiajing reign, Wang and Li founded the Seven Masters society, and Xie Zhen, though he was a commoner, was pushed aside.

sentences.zh: 渭憤其以軒冕壓韋布，誓不入二人黨。

translations.literal: Wei resented that they used official rank and court caps to crush commoners in hemp robes, and swore never to join the faction of the two men.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wei resented their use of official rank to crush men in plain cloth, and swore never to join the faction of the two.

sentences.zh: 後二十年，公安袁宏道遊越中，得渭殘帙以示祭酒陶望齡，相與激賞，刻其集行世。

translations.literal: Twenty years later, Yuan Hongdao of Gong'an traveled in Yue, obtained Wei's scattered remaining volumes and showed them to the Chancellor of the Imperial Academy Tao Wangling; together they praised them enthusiastically and had his collected works carved and published.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty years later, Yuan Hongdao of Gong'an traveled in Yue, found Wei's scattered remaining volumes, and showed them to Tao Wangling, Chancellor of the Imperial Academy; they praised them together and had his collected works printed and circulated.

sentences.zh: 寅，字仲房。

translations.literal: Yin, styled Zhongfang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yin, whose style name was Zhongfang.

sentences.zh: 明臣，字嘉則。

translations.literal: Mingchen, styled Jiaze.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Mingchen, whose style name was Jiaze.

sentences.zh: 皆有詩名。

translations.literal: Both had reputations for poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Both enjoyed reputations as poets.

sentences.zh: 屠隆者，字長卿，明臣同邑人也。

translations.literal: Tu Long, styled Changqing, was a fellow townsman of Mingchen.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Long, styled Changqing, was a fellow townsman of Shen Mingchen.

sentences.zh: 生有異才，嘗學詩於明臣，落筆數千言立就。

translations.literal: Born with unusual talent, he once studied poetry under Mingchen; when he put brush to paper several thousand words were completed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Born with unusual talent, he had once studied poetry under Shen Mingchen, and when he put brush to paper several thousand words would be completed at once.

sentences.zh: 族人大山、裏人張時徹方為貴官，共相延譽，名大噪。

translations.literal: His kinsman Dashan and fellow townsman Zhang Shiche, who were then high officials, together promoted his reputation, and his fame burst forth greatly.
translations.idiomatic: His kinsman Dashan and fellow townsman Zhang Shiche, who were then high officials, jointly praised him, and his fame spread far and wide.

sentences.zh: 舉萬歷五年進士，除潁上知縣，調繁青浦。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed magistrate of Yingshang, and was transferred to Qingpu, a demanding post.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Wanli, was appointed magistrate of Yingshang, and was transferred to the busy post of Qingpu.

sentences.zh: 時招名士飲酒賦詩，遊九峰、三泖，以仙令自許，然於吏事不廢，士民皆愛戴之。

translations.literal: He would summon famous scholars to drink wine and compose poetry, roam the Nine Peaks and Three Mo marshes, and style himself an immortal magistrate; yet he did not neglect official business, and officials and commoners alike loved and honored him.
translations.idiomatic: He would invite famous scholars to drink and compose poetry, roam the Nine Peaks and Three Mo marshes, and style himself an immortal magistrate; yet he never neglected official business, and both officials and commoners loved and respected him.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部主事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 西寧侯宋世恩兄事隆，宴遊甚歡。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Xining, Song Shi'en, treated Long as an elder brother, and they feasted and traveled together in great enjoyment.
translations.idiomatic: Song Shi'en, the Marquis of Xining, treated Tu Long as an elder brother, and they feasted and traveled together with great pleasure.

sentences.zh: 刑部主事俞顯卿者，險人也，嘗為隆所詆，心恨之。

translations.literal: Yu Xianqing, a principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice, was a treacherous man; Long had once denounced him, and he bore a grudge in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xianqing, a principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice, was a treacherous man; Tu Long had once denounced him, and he nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 訐隆與世恩淫縱，詞連禮部尚書陳經邦。

translations.literal: He denounced Long and Shi'en for debauchery and excess, and implicated Minister of Rites Chen Jingbang in the accusation.
translations.idiomatic: He accused Tu Long and Song Shi'en of debauchery and excess, and implicated Chen Jingbang, Minister of Rites, in the charge.

sentences.zh: 隆等上疏自理，並列顯卿挾仇誣陷狀。

translations.literal: Long and the others submitted memorials in self-defense, setting forth Xianqing's act of bearing a grudge and falsely framing them.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Long and the others submitted memorials in their own defense, detailing how Xianqing had borne a grudge and falsely framed them.

sentences.zh: 所司乃兩黜之，而停世恩俸半歲。

translations.literal: The responsible offices then dismissed both parties, and suspended Shi'en's salary for half a year.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices then dismissed both parties, and suspended Song Shi'en's salary for half a year.

sentences.zh: 隆歸，道青浦，父老為斂田千畝，請徙居。

translations.literal: When Long returned home and passed through Qingpu, the elders pooled together a thousand mu of fields and asked him to move there and live.
translations.idiomatic: On his way home Tu Long passed through Qingpu, where the elders pooled a thousand mu of fields and asked him to move there.

sentences.zh: 隆不許，歡飲三日謝去。

translations.literal: Long did not agree; after three days of joyful drinking he declined and left.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Long refused; after three days of merry drinking he thanked them and departed.

sentences.zh: 歸益縱情詩酒，好賓客，賣文為活。

translations.literal: Back home he gave himself ever more freely to poetry and wine, loved entertaining guests, and made a living by selling his writings.
translations.idiomatic: Once home he gave himself ever more freely to poetry and wine, loved entertaining guests, and made a living by selling his writings.

sentences.zh: 詩文率不經意，一揮數紙。

translations.literal: His poetry and prose were mostly composed without care; a few sweeps of the brush produced several sheets.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and prose were mostly dashed off without effort; a few sweeps of the brush would fill several sheets.

sentences.zh: 嘗戲命兩人對案拈二題，各賦百韻，咄嗟之間二章並就。

translations.literal: Once in jest he ordered two men facing each other across a desk to draw two topics and each compose a hundred-rhyme poem; in the space of a breath both pieces were finished.
translations.idiomatic: Once in jest he had two men sit facing each other, draw two topics, and each compose a hundred-rhyme poem; in a moment both pieces were finished.

sentences.zh: 又與人對弈，口誦詩文，命人書之，書不逮誦也。

translations.literal: Again, while playing chess with someone, he would recite poetry and prose aloud and have another person write it down; the writing could not keep pace with the recitation.
translations.idiomatic: He would also play chess with someone while reciting poetry and prose aloud and having another person write it down; the writing could not keep up with his recitation.

sentences.zh: 子婦沈氏，修撰懋學女，與隆女瑤瑟並能詩。

translations.literal: His daughter-in-law, Lady Shen, daughter of the Compiler Maoxue, and Long's daughter Yaose were both able to compose poetry.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter-in-law, Lady Shen, daughter of the compiler Maoxue, and Tu Long's daughter Yaose were both accomplished poets.

sentences.zh: 隆有所作，兩人輒和之。

translations.literal: Whenever Long produced a work, the two women would compose matching poems.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Tu Long wrote a poem, the two women would compose matching verses.

sentences.zh: 兩家兄弟合刻其詩，曰《留香草》。

translations.literal: The brothers of both families jointly carved their poems and titled the collection 《Fragrant Grass Left Behind》.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers of both families jointly published their poems under the title 《Fragrant Grass Left Behind》.

sentences.zh: 王穉登，字伯谷，長洲人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhideng, styled Bogu, was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhideng, whose style name was Bogu, was a native of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 四歲能屬對，六歲善擘窠大字，十歲能詩，長益駿發有盛名。

translations.literal: At four he could make parallel couplets; at six he was skilled at large seal-script characters; at ten he could compose poetry; as he grew his talent burst forth ever more brilliantly and he gained great fame.
translations.idiomatic: At four he could compose parallel couplets; at six he was skilled at large seal-script characters; at ten he could write poetry; as he grew his talent flourished ever more brilliantly and he gained great fame.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖末，遊京師，客大學士袁煒家。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jiajing reign he traveled to the capital and lodged in the home of Grand Secretary Yuan Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Jiajing reign he traveled to the capital and stayed as a guest in the home of Grand Secretary Yuan Wei.

sentences.zh: 煒試諸吉士紫牡丹詩，不稱意。

translations.literal: Wei tested the Hanlin academicians with a poem on purple peonies, but none pleased him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Wei tested the Hanlin academicians with a poem on purple peonies, but none satisfied him.

sentences.zh: 命穉登為之，有警句。

translations.literal: He ordered Zhideng to compose one; there were striking lines.
translations.idiomatic: He had Zhideng compose one, and it contained striking lines.

sentences.zh: 煒召數諸吉士曰：「君輩職文章，能得王秀才一句耶？」

translations.literal: Wei summoned several academicians and said: 「You gentlemen hold positions as men of letters—can you produce even one line like Scholar Wang's?
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Wei summoned several academicians and said: "You gentlemen are charged with literary work—can you produce even one line like Scholar Wang's?

sentences.zh: 將薦之朝，不果。

translations.literal: He was about to recommend him to the court, but it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to recommend him to the court, but the recommendation never went through.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，復遊京師，徐階當國，頗修憾於煒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Longqing reign he traveled to the capital again; Xu Jie held power and nursed considerable resentment toward Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longqing reign he traveled to the capital again; Xu Jie was directing state affairs and nursed considerable resentment toward Yuan Wei.

sentences.zh: 或勸穉登弗名袁公客，不從，刻《燕市》、《客越》二集，備書其事。

translations.literal: Some advised Zhideng not to style himself a client of Lord Yuan; he did not listen, and published the two collections 《Yanshi》 and 《Guest in Yue》, fully recording the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Some advised Zhideng not to style himself a client of Lord Yuan; he refused, and published the two collections 《Yanshi》 and 《Guest in Yue》, recording the whole affair in detail.

sentences.zh: 吳中自文征明後，風雅無定屬。

translations.literal: In Wu, after Wen Zhengming, there was no fixed master of refined letters.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wu region, after Wen Zhengming there was no settled leader of refined letters.

sentences.zh: 穉登嘗及征明門，遙接其風，主詞翰之席者三十余年。

translations.literal: Zhideng had once reached Zhengming's gate and from afar received his inspiration; he presided over the seat of literary composition for more than thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: Zhideng had once studied at Zhengming's gate and from afar received his influence; for more than thirty years he presided over the literary world.

sentences.zh: 嘉、隆、萬歷間，布衣、山人以詩名者十數，俞允文、王叔承、沈明臣輩尤為世所稱，然聲華烜赫，穉登為最。

translations.literal: Between the Jiajing, Longqing, and Wanli reigns, more than ten commoners and mountain recluses were famed for poetry; Yu Yunwen, Wang Shucheng, Shen Mingchen, and others were especially praised by the world, yet for splendor of reputation none matched Zhideng.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Jiajing, Longqing, and Wanli reigns, more than ten commoners and mountain recluses were famed for poetry; Yu Yunwen, Wang Shucheng, Shen Mingchen, and others were especially praised, yet for brilliance of reputation none matched Zhideng.

sentences.zh: 申時行以元老裏居，特相推重。

translations.literal: Shen Shixing, as a senior statesman living at home in his native place, especially honored and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Shixing, as a senior statesman living in retirement in his native place, especially honored and valued him.

sentences.zh: 王世貞與同郡友善，顧不甚推之。

translations.literal: Wang Shizhen, a fellow of the same commandery, was on friendly terms with him, but did not greatly promote him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shizhen, a fellow of the same commandery, was on friendly terms with him, but did not greatly promote his reputation.

sentences.zh: 及世貞歿，其仲子士骕坐事系獄，穉登為傾身救援，人以是重其風義。

translations.literal: When Shizhen died, his second son Shirun was imprisoned on account of an affair; Zhideng threw himself wholly into rescuing him, and people therefore respected his moral courage.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizhen died, his second son Shirun was imprisoned on account of a case; Zhideng threw himself wholly into rescuing him, and people respected him all the more for his moral courage.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中，詔修國史，大學士趙誌臯輩薦穉登及其同邑魏學禮、江都陸弼、黃岡王一鳴。

translations.literal: During Wanli, an edict ordered the compilation of the national history; Grand Secretary Zhao Zhigao and others recommended Zhideng, together with Wei Xueli of his native place, Lu Bi of Jiangdu, and Wang Yiming of Huanggang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign an edict ordered the compilation of the national history; Grand Secretary Zhao Zhigao and others recommended Zhideng, together with Wei Xueli of his native place, Lu Bi of Jiangdu, and Wang Yiming of Huanggang.

sentences.zh: 有詔征用，未上，而史局罷。

translations.literal: There was an edict summoning them for appointment, but before they reported the history office was dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned them for appointment, but before they reported the history office was dissolved.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十余。

translations.literal: He died at over seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died at over seventy years of age.

sentences.zh: 子留，字亦房，亦以詩名。

translations.literal: His son Liu, styled Yifang, was also famed for poetry.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu, whose style name was Yifang, was also famed for his poetry.

sentences.zh: 俞允文，字仲蔚，昆山人。

translations.literal: Yu Yunwen, styled Zhongwei, was a native of Kunshan.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yunwen, whose style name was Zhongwei, was a native of Kunshan.

sentences.zh: 其父舉進士，官大理評事。

translations.literal: His father passed the jinshi examination and served as a reviewing official in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: His father had passed the jinshi examination and served as a reviewing official in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 允文年十五為《馬鞍山賦》，援據該博。

translations.literal: At fifteen Yunwen wrote the 《Rhapsody on Mount Ma'an》, with citations broad and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen Yunwen wrote the 《Rhapsody on Mount Ma'an》, with citations that were broad and thorough.

sentences.zh: 年未四十，謝去諸生，專力於詩文書法。

translations.literal: Before he was forty he withdrew from being a student, and devoted himself entirely to poetry, prose, and calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Before he was forty he gave up his status as a student and devoted himself entirely to poetry, prose, and calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 與王世貞善，而不喜李攀龍詩，其持論不茍同如此。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Wang Shizhen but did not care for Li Panlong's poetry; such was his independent-mindedness in debate.
translations.idiomatic: He was on good terms with Wang Shizhen but did not care for Li Panlong's poetry; such was his unwillingness to agree uncritically.

sentences.zh: 王叔承，字承父，吳江人。

translations.literal: Wang Shucheng, styled Chengfu, was a native of Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shucheng, whose style name was Chengfu, was a native of Wujiang.

sentences.zh: 少孤，治經生業，以好古謝去。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he pursued the study of classicist learning but withdrew because of his love of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he pursued the study of classicist learning but withdrew because of his love of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 貧，贅婦家，為婦翁所遂，不予一錢，乃攜婦歸奉母，貧益甚。

translations.literal: Poor, he married into his wife's family; his father-in-law sent him away and gave him not a single coin; he took his wife back to serve his mother, and his poverty grew worse still.
translations.idiomatic: Poor, he married into his wife's family; his father-in-law sent him away without giving him a single coin; he took his wife home to serve his mother, and his poverty grew worse still.

sentences.zh: 入都，客大學士李春芳所。

translations.literal: He entered the capital and lodged with Grand Secretary Li Chunfang.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the capital and stayed as a guest with Grand Secretary Li Chunfang.

sentences.zh: 性嗜酒，春芳有所撰述，覓之，往往臥酒樓，欠伸弗肯應。

translations.literal: By nature he loved wine; when Chunfang had something to compose and sought him out, he would often be lying drunk in a wine shop, stretching lazily and refusing to respond.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved wine; when Li Chunfang had something to compose and sought him out, he would often be lying drunk in a wine shop, stretching lazily and refusing to answer.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃謝歸。

translations.literal: After a long while he took leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he took his leave and returned home.

sentences.zh: 太倉王錫爵，其布衣交也。

translations.literal: Wang Xijue of Taicang was his friend when both were commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xijue of Taicang had been his friend when both were commoners.

sentences.zh: 再召，會有三王並封之議，叔承遺書數千言，謂當引大義以去就力爭，不當依違兩端，負主恩，辜物望。

translations.literal: When summoned again, there happened to be discussion of enfeoffing three princes simultaneously; Shucheng sent a letter of several thousand words, saying one should appeal to grand principle and struggle to the utmost with one's stay or withdrawal, and should not waver between two sides, betray the sovereign's grace, and disappoint public expectation.
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned again, there happened to be discussion of enfeoffing three princes simultaneously; Shucheng sent a letter of several thousand words, saying one should appeal to grand principle and fight to the utmost over whether to stay or withdraw, and should not waver between two sides, betray the sovereign's grace, and disappoint public expectation.

sentences.zh: 錫爵得書嘆服。

translations.literal: Xijue received the letter and sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xijue received the letter and sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 其詩，極為世貞兄弟所許。

translations.literal: His poetry was highly approved by the brothers Wang Shizhen.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry was highly praised by the brothers Wang Shizhen.

sentences.zh: 卒於萬歷中。

translations.literal: He died during the Wanli period.
translations.idiomatic: He died during the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 瞿九思，字睿夫，黃梅人。

translations.literal: Qu Jiusi, styled Ruifu, was a native of Huangmei.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Jiusi, whose style name was Ruifu, was a native of Huangmei.

sentences.zh: 父晟，嘉靖三十二年進士。

translations.literal: His father Sheng passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-second year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sheng passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-second year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 歷官廣平知府。

translations.literal: He served in succession as prefect of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: He held office in succession as prefect of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 鑿長渠三百里，引水為四閘，得田數十萬畝。

translations.literal: He dug a long canal three hundred li, drew water through four sluice gates, and brought under cultivation several hundred thousand mu of fields.
translations.idiomatic: He dug a long canal three hundred li long, drew water through four sluice gates, and brought several hundred thousand mu of fields under cultivation.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died while in office.

sentences.zh: 九思十歲從父宦吉安，事羅洪先。

translations.literal: At ten Jiusi followed his father on official service to Ji'an and studied under Luo Hongxian.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of ten Jiusi followed his father on official service to Ji'an and studied under Luo Hongxian.

sentences.zh: 十五作《定誌論》。

translations.literal: At fifteen he wrote the 《On Fixing the Will》.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of fifteen he wrote the 《On Fixing the Will》.

sentences.zh: 後從同郡耿定向遊，學益進。

translations.literal: Later he traveled with Geng Dingxiang of the same commandery, and his learning advanced further.
translations.idiomatic: Later he studied with Geng Dingxiang of the same commandery, and his learning advanced further.

sentences.zh: 舉萬歷元年鄉試。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination in the first year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the first year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 居二年，縣令張維翰違制苛派，民聚毆之，維翰坐九思倡亂。

translations.literal: Two years later the county magistrate Zhang Weihan made illegal harsh levies; the people gathered and beat him; Weihan blamed Jiusi for inciting disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the county magistrate Zhang Weihan made illegal harsh levies; the people gathered and beat him, and Weihan blamed Jiusi for inciting the disorder.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史向程劾維翰激變。

translations.literal: The touring censor Xiang Cheng impeached Weihan for provoking the upheaval.
translations.idiomatic: The touring censor Xiang Cheng impeached Zhang Weihan for provoking the upheaval.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書張瀚言御史議非是，九思遂長流塞下。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Zhang Han said the censor's judgment was wrong, and Jiusi was then sentenced to long exile on the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Zhang Han said the censor's judgment was incorrect, and Jiusi was then sentenced to long exile on the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 子甲，年十三，為書數千言，歷抵公卿，訟父冤。

translations.literal: His son Jia, at thirteen, wrote a letter of several thousand words, went from one high official to another, and pleaded his father's innocence.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jia, at the age of thirteen, wrote a letter of several thousand words, went from one high official to another, and pleaded his father's innocence.

sentences.zh: 甲弟罕，亦伏闕上書求宥。

translations.literal: Jia's younger brother Han also prostrated himself before the palace gate and submitted a memorial seeking pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Jia's younger brother Han also prostrated himself before the palace gate and submitted a memorial asking for pardon.

sentences.zh: 屠隆作《訟瞿生書》，遍告中外，馮夢禎亦白於楚中當事，而張居正故才九思，乃獲釋歸。

translations.literal: Tu Long wrote the 《Petition on Behalf of Scholar Qu》, informing officials at home and abroad; Feng Mengzhen also pleaded on his behalf to the authorities in Chu; and because Zhang Juzheng had long valued Jiusi's talent, he was finally released and allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Long wrote the 《Petition on Behalf of Scholar Qu》, informing officials at home and abroad; Feng Mengzhen also pleaded on his behalf to the authorities in Chu; and because Zhang Juzheng had long valued Jiusi's talent, he was finally released and allowed to return home.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，以撫按疏薦，授翰林待詔，力辭不受。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year, on recommendation in a memorial from the governor and inspector, he was appointed Hanlin awaiting imperial decree, but firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year, on the recommendation of the governor and inspector in a memorial, he was appointed Hanlin awaiting imperial decree, but firmly declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 詔有司歲給米六十石，終其身。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the local offices to grant him sixty shi of grain yearly for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the local offices to grant him sixty shi of grain each year for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 乃撰《樂章》及《萬歷武功錄》，遣罕詣闕上之。

translations.literal: He then compiled the 《Musical Compositions》 and the 《Record of Wanli Military Achievements》, and sent Han to the palace gate to submit them.
translations.idiomatic: He then compiled the 《Musical Compositions》 and the 《Record of Wanli Military Achievements》, and sent Han to the palace to submit them.

sentences.zh: 卒年七十一。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 九思學極奧博，其文章不雅馴，然一時嗜古篤誌之士亦鮮其儔。

translations.literal: Jiusi's learning was extremely profound and vast; his writings were not elegant and docile, yet among lovers of antiquity and men of earnest purpose in that age few could match him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiusi's learning was extremely profound and vast; his writings were not elegant and tame, yet among lovers of antiquity and men of earnest purpose in that age few could match him.

sentences.zh: 甲，字釋之，年十九舉於鄉，早卒。

translations.literal: Jia, styled Shizhi, passed the provincial examination at nineteen and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Jia, whose style name was Shizhi, passed the provincial examination at nineteen and died young.

sentences.zh: 罕，字曰有，七歲能文。

translations.literal: Han, styled Riyou, could write at seven.
translations.idiomatic: Han, whose style name was Riyou, could write at the age of seven.

sentences.zh: 白父冤時，往返徒步，不避寒餒，天下稱雙孝。

translations.literal: When they pleaded their father's innocence, they traveled back and forth on foot, not avoiding cold and hunger; all under heaven called them the Two Filial Sons.
translations.idiomatic: When they pleaded their father's innocence, they traveled back and forth on foot without avoiding cold and hunger; all under heaven called them the Two Filial Sons.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，辟舉知州。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen period he was summoned by recommendation and appointed prefect.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign he was summoned by recommendation and appointed prefect.

sentences.zh: 唐時升，字叔達，嘉定人。

translations.literal: Tang Shisheng, styled Shuda, was a native of Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Shisheng, whose style name was Shuda, was a native of Jiading.

sentences.zh: 父欽訓，與歸有光善，故時升早登有光之門。

translations.literal: His father Qinxun was on good terms with Gui Youguang, so Shisheng early entered Youguang's school.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qinxun was on good terms with Gui Youguang, so Shisheng entered Youguang's school at an early age.

sentences.zh: 年未三十，謝舉子業，專意古學。

translations.literal: Before he was thirty he gave up the pursuit of examination essays and devoted himself entirely to ancient learning.
translations.idiomatic: Before he was thirty he gave up the pursuit of examination essays and devoted himself wholly to ancient learning.

sentences.zh: 王世貞官南都，延之邸舍，與辨晰疑義。

translations.literal: When Wang Shizhen served in the southern capital, he invited him to his residence and discussed difficult points to clarify their meaning.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shizhen served in the southern capital, he invited him to his residence and discussed difficult points in order to clarify their meaning.

sentences.zh: 時升自以出歸氏門，不肯復稱王氏弟子。

translations.literal: Shisheng considered himself a product of the Gui school and refused to style himself Wang's disciple again.
translations.idiomatic: Shisheng considered himself a product of the Gui school and refused to call himself Wang's disciple again.

sentences.zh: 及王錫爵枋國，其子衡邀時升入都，值塞上用兵，逆斷其情形虛實，將帥勝負，無一爽者。

translations.literal: When Wang Xijue directed state affairs, his son Heng invited Shisheng to the capital; there happened to be military action on the northern frontier, and he foretold the actual situation—what was real and what was not—and the victories and defeats of commanders, without a single error.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Xijue directed state affairs, his son Heng invited Shisheng to the capital; there happened to be military action on the northern frontier, and he foretold the actual situation, the truth and falsehood of reports, and the victories and defeats of commanders, without a single error.

sentences.zh: 家貧，好施予，灌園藝蔬，蕭然自得。

translations.literal: His family was poor but he loved to give; he watered the garden and cultivated vegetables, content in austere simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Though his family was poor he loved to give; he watered the garden and cultivated vegetables, content in austere simplicity.

sentences.zh: 詩援筆成，不加點竄，文得有光之傳。

translations.literal: His poetry came from the brush complete without revision; his prose inherited Youguang's tradition.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry came from the brush complete without revision; his prose inherited Youguang's literary tradition.

sentences.zh: 與裏人婁堅、程嘉燧並稱曰「練川三老」。

translations.literal: Together with his fellow townsman Lou Jian and Cheng Jiasui he was collectively called 「The Three Elders of Lianchuan」.
translations.idiomatic: Together with his fellow townsman Lou Jian and Cheng Jiasui he was collectively known as "The Three Elders of Lianchuan."

sentences.zh: 卒於崇禎九年，年八十有六。

translations.literal: He died in the ninth year of Chongzhen, at the age of eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year of the Chongzhen reign, at the age of eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 婁堅，字子柔。

translations.literal: Lou Jian, styled Zirou.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Jian, whose style name was Zirou.

sentences.zh: 幼好學，其師友皆出有光門。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning; his teachers and friends all came from Youguang's school.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning; his teachers and friends all came from Gui Youguang's school.

sentences.zh: 堅學有師承，經明行修，鄉里推為大師。

translations.literal: Jian's learning had teacher transmission; his understanding of the classics was clear and his conduct cultivated; the locality esteemed him as a great master.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had true lineage in his studies—clear mastery of the classics and exemplary conduct—and his community hailed him as a master scholar.

sentences.zh: 貢於國學，不仕而歸。

translations.literal: He presented himself as tribute scholar at the National Academy, then returned without taking office.
translations.idiomatic: He presented himself for study at the Imperial Academy but returned home without entering government service.

sentences.zh: 工書法，詩亦清新。

translations.literal: He was skilled at calligraphy; his poetry was also fresh and lucid.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at calligraphy, and his poetry was likewise fresh and lucid.

sentences.zh: 四明謝三賓知縣事，合時升、堅、嘉燧及李流芳詩刻之，曰《嘉定四先生集》。

translations.literal: Xie Sanbin of Siming, while serving as magistrate, combined the poems of Shi Sheng, Jian, Jiasui, and Li Liufang and had them carved for printing, titling it 《Collected Works of the Four Masters of Jiading》.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as magistrate of Siming, Xie Sanbin collected and published the poetry of Shi Sheng, Lou Jian, Cheng Jiasui, and Li Liufang under the title 《Collected Works of the Four Masters of Jiading》.

sentences.zh: 流芳，字長蘅，萬歷三十四年舉於鄉。

translations.literal: Liufang, styled Changheng, passed the provincial examination in the thirty-fourth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liufang, styled Changheng, passed the provincial examination in the thirty-fourth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 工詩善書，尤精繪事。

translations.literal: He was skilled at poetry and good at writing; he was especially expert at painting.
translations.idiomatic: He was accomplished in poetry and calligraphy and especially distinguished as a painter.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，會試北上，抵近郊聞警，賦詩而返，遂絕意進取。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi, he went north for the metropolitan examination; reaching the suburbs he heard the alarm, composed poetry and returned, then utterly abandoned intent to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign he set out north for the metropolitan examination, but on reaching the suburbs he heard news of an emergency, wrote a poem, and turned back—after which he abandoned all ambition for official advancement.

sentences.zh: 程嘉燧，字孟陽，休寧人，僑居嘉定。

translations.literal: Cheng Jiasui, styled Mengyang, was a native of Xiuning, residing by sojourn in Jiading.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Jiasui, styled Mengyang, was a native of Xiuning who lived in Jiading as a resident outsider.

sentences.zh: 工詩善畫。

translations.literal: He was skilled at poetry and good at painting.
translations.idiomatic: He was accomplished in both poetry and painting.

sentences.zh: 與通州顧養謙善。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Gu Yangqian of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was close friends with Gu Yangqian of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 友人勸詣之，乃渡江寓古寺，與酒人歡飲三日夜，賦《詠古》五章，不見養謙而返。

translations.literal: Friends urged him to call on him; thereupon he crossed the river and lodged in an old temple, with wine companions reveled and drank three days and nights, composed five chapters of 《On the Ancient》, did not see Yangqian and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When friends urged him to visit Gu, he crossed the Yangtze and stayed in an old temple, where he caroused with drinking companions for three days and nights, wrote five poems titled 《On the Ancient》, and then returned without ever calling on Yangqian.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，常熟錢謙益以侍郎罷歸，築耦耕堂，邀嘉燧讀書其中。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen period, Qian Qianyi of Changshu, dismissed from office as vice minister, built the Hall of Coupled Plowing, and invited Jiasui to study therein.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign, Qian Qianyi of Changshu returned home after being dismissed from his post as vice minister and built the Hall of Coupled Plowing, inviting Jiasui to join him there for scholarly retreat.

sentences.zh: 閱十年返休寧，遂卒，年七十有九。

translations.literal: After ten years he returned to Xiuning, then died, age seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years he returned to Xiuning, where he soon died at the age of seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 謙益最重其詩，稱曰松圓詩老。

translations.literal: Qianyi most valued his poetry, calling him the Old Master of Songyuan's Poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Qianyi held his poetry in the highest regard and called him the Old Master of the Pine Garden Poets.

sentences.zh: 焦竑，字弱侯，江寧人。

translations.literal: Jiao Hong, styled Ruohou, was a native of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Hong, styled Ruohou, was a native of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 為諸生，有盛名。

translations.literal: As a county school student, he had great fame.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a county school student he enjoyed wide renown.

sentences.zh: 從督學御史耿定向學，復質疑於羅汝芳。

translations.literal: He studied under Supervising Censor Geng Dingxiang, and again raised doubts for discussion with Luo Rufang.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under the provincial education commissioner Geng Dingxiang and also sought out Luo Rufang to discuss his questions.

sentences.zh: 舉嘉靖四十三年鄉試，下第還。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year of Jiajing he entered the provincial examination, failed, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He took the provincial examination in the forty-third year of Jiajing, failed, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 定向遴十四郡名士讀書崇正書院，以竑為之長。

translations.literal: Dingxiang selected notable scholars of fourteen prefectures to study at the Chongzheng Academy, making Hong their head.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxiang selected leading scholars from fourteen prefectures to study at the Chongzheng Academy and appointed Hong their head.

sentences.zh: 及定向裏居，復往從之。

translations.literal: When Dingxiang retired to his home district, Hong again went to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: When Dingxiang retired to his home district, Hong again went to study under him.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十七年，始以殿試第一人官翰林修撰，益討習國朝典章。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Wanli, he first took office as Hanlin Compiler as top passed of the palace examination, and further studied the court statutes and regulations of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Wanli he at last ranked first in the palace examination and was appointed Hanlin Compiler, devoting himself ever more to mastering the institutions and regulations of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，大學士陳於陛建議修國史，欲竑專領其事，竑遜謝，乃先撰《經籍志》，其他率無所撰，館亦竟罷。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, Grand Secretary Chen Yubi proposed revising the national history, wishing Hong to specially lead the matter; Hong modestly declined, then first drafted the 《Bibliographical Treatise》, on the rest generally wrote nothing, and the bureau was ultimately dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Grand Secretary Chen Yubi proposed compiling a national history and wanted Hong to head the project, but Hong modestly declined. He did draft the 《Bibliographical Treatise》, but contributed little else, and the editorial bureau was eventually dissolved.

sentences.zh: 翰林教小內侍書者，眾視為具文，竑獨曰：「此曹他日在帝左右，安得忽之。」

translations.literal: Hanlin instructors who taught young eunuchs writing—everyone regarded it as empty formality; Hong alone said: 「These people one day will be at the Emperor's side—how can one treat them lightly?
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin instructors assigned to teach palace eunuchs calligraphy treated the duty as a mere formality, but Hong alone said: 「These men will one day stand at the Emperor's side—how can we neglect their education?

sentences.zh: 取古奄人善惡，時與論說。

translations.literal: 」He took the good and evil of eunuchs of antiquity and from time to time discussed them.
translations.idiomatic: He would draw on stories of good and wicked eunuchs from antiquity and discuss them with his pupils from time to time.

sentences.zh: 皇長子出閣，竑為講官。

translations.literal: When the crown prince left the palace precinct, Hong became his lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince was formally established in his own residence, Hong became one of his lecturers.

sentences.zh: 故事，講官進講罕有問者。

translations.literal: By precedent, when lecturing officials entered to lecture, rarely was there one who questioned.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, lecturers rarely received questions from the crown prince after delivering their lectures.

sentences.zh: 竑講畢，徐曰：「博學審問，功用維均，敷陳或未盡，惟殿下賜明問。」

translations.literal: When Hong finished lecturing, he said slowly: 「Broad learning and careful questioning—their functions are equally important; my exposition may not have been complete—may Your Highness bestow clarifying questions.
translations.idiomatic: After finishing a lecture, Hong would say gently: 「Learning broadly and questioning carefully serve the same purpose. I may not have explained everything fully—I hope Your Highness will honor me with your questions.

sentences.zh: 皇長子稱善，然無所質難也。

translations.literal: 」The crown prince praised it, yet had nothing to question or challenge.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince would praise him, but still never asked a question.

sentences.zh: 一日，竑復進曰：「殿下言不易發，得毋諱其誤耶？

translations.literal: One day, Hong again advanced and said: 「Your Highness's words are not easily spoken—could it be that you are concealing error?
translations.idiomatic: One day Hong pressed again: 「Your Highness seldom speaks up—is it because you fear being wrong?

sentences.zh: 解則有誤，問復何誤？

translations.literal: Explaining, there can be error; questioning, again what error?
translations.idiomatic: In explaining there may be mistakes, but in asking questions, what mistake is there?

sentences.zh: 古人不恥下問，願以為法。」

translations.literal: The ancients did not consider it shameful to question those below them; I wish to take this as model.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients were not ashamed to ask those beneath them for instruction—I hope Your Highness will take them as your model.

sentences.zh: 皇長子復稱善，亦竟無所問。

translations.literal: 」The crown prince again praised it, yet in the end still had no questions.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince praised him again but still never asked anything.

sentences.zh: 竑乃與同列謀先啟其端，適講《舜典》，竑舉「稽於眾，舍己從人」為問。

translations.literal: Hong then with his colleagues schemed to first open the beginning for him; just then lecturing on the 《Canon of Shun》, Hong raised 「investigate among the multitude, set aside oneself and follow others」 as a question.
translations.idiomatic: Hong then conspired with his fellow lecturers to break the ice: while lecturing on the 《Canon of Shun》, he prompted the crown prince with the passage 「consult the people widely and set aside your own views to follow what is better in others.」

sentences.zh: 皇長子曰：「稽者，考也。

translations.literal: The crown prince said: 「Ji means examine.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince replied: 「Ji means to examine.

sentences.zh: 考集眾思，然後舍己之短，從人之長。」

translations.literal: Examine and gather the thoughts of the multitude; then set aside one's own shortcomings and follow others' strengths.
translations.idiomatic: One gathers the thoughts of the people, then sets aside one's own shortcomings and follows others' strengths.

sentences.zh: 又一日，舉「上帝降衷，若有恒性」。

translations.literal: 」Another day, he raised 「The Supreme Lord sent down the inmost heart, as if there were constant nature.」
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion he prompted him with the line 「God sent down the inmost heart, as if imparting a constant nature.」

sentences.zh: 皇長子曰：「此無他，即天命之謂性也。」

translations.literal: The crown prince said: 「This is nothing else—it is what is called nature as Heaven's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince said: 「This means nothing else—it is what Mencius called nature as the mandate of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 時方十三齡，答問無滯，竑亦竭誠啟迪。

translations.literal: 」At that time he was just thirteen years of age; in answering questions there was no hesitation; Hong also with all sincerity enlightened him.
translations.idiomatic: He was only thirteen at the time, yet answered without hesitation, and Hong in turn devoted himself wholeheartedly to guiding him.

sentences.zh: 嘗講次，群鳥飛鳴，皇長子仰視，竑輟講肅立。

translations.literal: Once during a lecture, a flock of birds flew crying; the crown prince looked up; Hong ceased lecturing and stood solemnly.
translations.idiomatic: Once during a lecture a flock of birds flew overhead calling; the crown prince looked up, and Hong stopped speaking and stood at attention.

sentences.zh: 皇長子斂容聽，乃復講如初。

translations.literal: The crown prince composed his countenance and listened; then Hong resumed lecturing as before.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince composed himself and turned back to listen, Hong resumed the lecture as before.

sentences.zh: 竑嘗采古儲君事可為法戒者為《養正圖說》，擬進之。

translations.literal: Hong once collected affairs of crown princes of antiquity that could serve as models and warnings, making the 《Illustrated Discourse on Cultivating Rectitude》, intending to present it.
translations.idiomatic: Hong once compiled stories of crown princes from antiquity that could serve as models or warnings into the 《Illustrated Discourse on Cultivating Rectitude》, which he intended to submit to the throne.

sentences.zh: 同官郭正域輩惡其不相聞，目為賈譽，竑遂止。

translations.literal: Colleagues such as Guo Zhengyu resented that he had not informed them, viewed him as trafficking in praise; Hong then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues such as Guo Zhengyu resented his not having consulted them and accused him of currying favor; Hong abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 竑既負重名，性復疏直，時事有不可，輒形之言論，政府亦惡之，張位尤甚。

translations.literal: Hong already bore heavy fame, and his nature was again blunt and straight; when current affairs had what was not permissible, he promptly gave it form in discourse; the government also hated this, Zhang Wei especially so.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Hong enjoyed enormous renown and was blunt by nature; whenever he saw something wrong in public affairs he spoke out openly, which the court resented—especially Grand Secretary Zhang Wei.

sentences.zh: 二十五年主順天鄉試，舉子曹蕃等九人文多險誕語，竑被劾，謫福寧州同知。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he presided over the Shuntian provincial examination; examinees Cao Fan and nine others had essays with much dangerous and extravagant language; Hong was impeached and demoted to assistant prefect of Funing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year, while chief examiner for the Shuntian provincial examination, he was impeached because nine candidates including Cao Fan had submitted essays full of dangerous and extravagant language; he was demoted to assistant prefect of Funing.

sentences.zh: 歲餘大計，復鐫秩，竑遂不出。

translations.literal: After a year plus the grand assessment, his rank was again reduced; Hong then did not emerge.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a year his rank was reduced again in the triennial review, and Hong never returned to office.

sentences.zh: 竑博極群書，自經史至稗官、雜說，無不淹貫。

translations.literal: Hong exhaustively reached myriad books, from classics and histories down to unofficial histories and miscellaneous writings—nothing not thoroughly penetrated.
translations.idiomatic: Hong read exhaustively across the entire range of literature, from the classics and dynastic histories to unofficial histories and miscellaneous writings—there was nothing he had not mastered.

sentences.zh: 善為古文，典正馴雅，卓然名家。

translations.literal: He was good at composing ancient-style prose; canonical, correct, tame and refined—standing out as a master of his school.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote ancient-style prose with canonical dignity and restrained elegance and stands as a master in his own right.

sentences.zh: 集名《淡園》，竑所自號也。

translations.literal: His collection was named 《Danyuan》—Hong's self-adopted style-name.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works were titled 《The Tranquil Garden》—Danyuan being the name he gave himself.

sentences.zh: 講學以汝芳為宗，而善定向兄弟及李贄，時頗以禪學譏之。

translations.literal: In lecturing his learning he took Rufang as patriarch, yet was on good terms with the Dingxiang brothers and Li Zhi; at the time many with Chan learning ridiculed him.
translations.idiomatic: In his teaching he took Luo Rufang as his guide and was close to the Dingxiang brothers and Li Zhi, though many at the time mocked him for leaning toward Chan Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十八年卒，年八十。

translations.literal: In the forty-eighth year of Wanli he died, age eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the forty-eighth year of Wanli at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 熹宗時，以先朝講讀恩，復官，贈諭德，賜祭蔭子。

translations.literal: In the Xizong reign, by grace of lecture and reading in the previous court, his office was restored; he was posthumously granted Junior Mentor; sacrificial rites and hereditary privilege for his son were bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tianqi emperor he was posthumously reinstated in recognition of his service lecturing the crown prince, granted the posthumous title of Junior Mentor, and his son received sacrificial honors and hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 福王時，追謚文端。

translations.literal: In the Fu Prince's time, posthumously ennobled with posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Southern Ming Prince of Fu he was posthumously given the temple name Wenduan (Cultured and Upright).

sentences.zh: 子潤生，見《忠義傳》。

translations.literal: His son Runsheng—see the 《Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness》.
translations.idiomatic: His son Runsheng is treated in the 《Biographies of Loyalty and Righteousness》.

sentences.zh: 黃輝，字平倩，一字昭素，南充人。

translations.literal: Huang Hui, styled Pingqian, also styled Zhaosu, was a native of Nanchong.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hui, styled Pingqian and also Zhaosu, was a native of Nanchong.

sentences.zh: 竑同年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the same year as Hong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the same year as Jiao Hong.

sentences.zh: 幼穎異，父子元，官湖廣，御史屬訊疑獄，輝檢律如老吏。

translations.literal: From youth he was exceptionally bright; his father Ziyuan held office in Huguang; the censor assigned him to interrogate doubtful cases; Hui examined the laws like an old clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Exceptionally bright from childhood, while his father Ziyuan served in Huguang the boy was asked by a supervising censor to help examine doubtful cases—and parsed the legal codes like a veteran clerk.

sentences.zh: 御史聞而異之，命負以至，授錢谷集，一覽輒記。

translations.literal: The censor heard and wondered at this, ordered him carried to come; gave him the treasury and grain documents; one glance and he remembered.
translations.idiomatic: Astonished, the censor had him brought in and handed him a register of tax and grain receipts, which the boy memorized at a single reading.

sentences.zh: 稍長，博極群書。

translations.literal: When slightly grown, he exhaustively reached myriad books.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older he devoured books across every field.

sentences.zh: 年十五舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: At age fifteen he entered the provincial examination first.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he ranked first in the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 久之，成進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: After a long time, he completed as jinshi, was transferred to Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: Some years later he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 館課文字多沿襲熟爛，目為翰林體，及李攀龍、王世貞之學行，則又改而從之。

translations.literal: Academy assignment compositions mostly followed worn patterns of stale overripeness, called the Hanlin style; when Li Panlong and Wang Shizhen's learning flourished, then again he changed and followed them.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin trainees typically wrote in a stale, formulaic Academy style, but when the archaist school of Li Panlong and Wang Shizhen rose to prominence, he too switched and followed their lead.

sentences.zh: 輝刻意學古，一以韓、歐為師，館閣文稍變。

translations.literal: Hui deliberately studied antiquity, taking Han and Ou alone as teachers; Academy and court prose slightly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Hui deliberately turned to antiquity, taking Han Yu and Ouyang Xiu as his sole models, and Academy prose began to shift.

sentences.zh: 時同館中，詩文推陶望齡，書畫推董其昌，輝詩及書與齊名。

translations.literal: At the time among fellows of the same academy, in poetry and prose Tao Wangling was esteemed; in calligraphy and painting Dong Qichang was esteemed; Hui's poetry and writing together held equal fame.
translations.idiomatic: Among his Hanlin cohort Tao Wangling was ranked first in poetry and prose and Dong Qichang in calligraphy and painting, but Hui's poetry and calligraphy matched either man's reputation.

sentences.zh: 至征事，輝十得八九，竑以閎雅名，亦自遜不如也。

translations.literal: As for citing affairs, Hui got eight or nine out of ten; Hong was famed for broad elegance, yet also modestly yielded that he was not as good.
translations.idiomatic: When it came to marshaling historical allusions, Hui was right eight or nine times out of ten—even Jiao Hong, famed for his broad erudition, conceded he could not match him.

sentences.zh: 由編修遷右中允，充皇長子講官。

translations.literal: From compiler he was transferred to Right Attendant-in-Waiting, filling the post of crown prince lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from compiler to Right Attendant-in-Waiting and served as a lecturer to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 時帝寵鄭貴妃，疏皇后、長子，長子生母王恭妃幾殆。

translations.literal: At the time the Emperor favored Noble Consort Zheng, kept distant the empress and crown prince; the crown prince's birth mother, Honored Consort Wang, nearly perished.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor favored Lady Zheng, neglected the empress and crown prince, and the crown prince's mother, Lady Wang, was nearly brought to ruin.

sentences.zh: 輝從內豎征知其狀，謂同里給事中王德完曰：「此國家大事，旦夕不測，書之史冊，謂朝廷無人，吾輩為萬世僇矣。」

translations.literal: Hui from inner eunuchs inquired and knew the situation; he said to fellow townsman supervising secretary Wang Dewan: 「This is a great affair of state; day or night unforeseeable; written in the historical annals that the court had no men—we would become the laughingstock of ten thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: Learning the situation from palace eunuchs, he told his fellow townsman Wang Dewan, a supervising secretary: 「This is a matter of state. Anything may happen at any moment. If history records that the court had no one willing to act, we will be shamed for all time.

sentences.zh: 德完奮然，屬輝具草上之，下獄，廷杖瀕死。

translations.literal: 」Dewan was roused; he entrusted Hui to draft a memorial and submit it; Dewan was imprisoned, court beaten nearly to death.
translations.idiomatic: Wang resolutely commissioned Hui to draft a memorial and submit it. Wang was thrown into prison and nearly beaten to death in a court flogging.

sentences.zh: 輝周旋橐饘，不避險阻，人或危之。

translations.literal: Hui went back and forth with provisions in his bag, not avoiding danger and obstruction; some people warned him of peril.
translations.idiomatic: Hui went back and forth bringing him food and supplies, undeterred by the risk, though others warned him he was in danger.

sentences.zh: 輝曰：「吾陷人於禍，可坐視乎？」

translations.literal: Hui said: 「I entangled a man in calamity—can I sit and watch?
translations.idiomatic: Hui said: 「I drew him into this disaster—how can I stand by and do nothing?

sentences.zh: 輝雅好禪學，多方外交，為言者所論。

translations.literal: 」Hui by nature loved Chan learning, in many ways had outside contacts; he was attacked by censors.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was deeply drawn to Chan Buddhism and maintained wide contacts outside official circles, which drew censure from the censoriate.

sentences.zh: 時已為庶子掌司經局，遂請告歸。

translations.literal: At the time he was already Junior Mentor in charge of the Classics Bureau; thereupon he requested leave and returned.
translations.idiomatic: By then he was Junior Mentor in charge of the Classics Bureau; he resigned and returned home.

sentences.zh: 已，起故官，擢少詹事兼侍讀學士，卒官。

translations.literal: Later, recalled to former office, promoted to Junior Vice Director of the Hanlin Academy concurrently Reader-in-Waiting, died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled, promoted to Junior Vice Director of the Hanlin Academy and Reader-in-Waiting, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 陳仁錫，字明卿，長洲人。

translations.literal: Chen Renxi, styled Mingqing, was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Renxi, styled Mingqing, was a native of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 父允堅，進士。

translations.literal: His father Yunjian was a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yunjian had passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 歷知諸暨、崇德二縣。

translations.literal: He successively served as magistrate of Zhuji and Chongde two counties.
translations.idiomatic: He had served successively as magistrate of Zhuji and Chongde.

sentences.zh: 仁錫年十九，舉萬歷二十五年鄉試。

translations.literal: Renxi at age nineteen entered the provincial examination of the twenty-fifth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Renxi passed the provincial examination at nineteen in the twenty-fifth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 聞武進錢一本善《易》，往師之，得其指要。

translations.literal: Hearing that Qian Yiben of Wujin was skilled in the 《Changes》, he went to take him as teacher and obtained its essential pointers.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Qian Yiben of Wujin was master of the Book of Changes, he went to study under him and grasped its essentials.

sentences.zh: 久不第。

translations.literal: For long he did not pass.
translations.idiomatic: For many years he failed to pass the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 益究心經史之學，多所論著。

translations.literal: He further devoted his mind to the learning of classics and histories, with much writing and discussion.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself ever more deeply to the classics and histories and produced a substantial body of scholarly writing.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年以殿試第三人授翰林編修。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi, as third-ranked of the palace examination he was appointed Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianqi he ranked third in the palace examination and was appointed Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 時第一為文震孟，亦老成宿學。

translations.literal: At the time the first was Wen Zhenmeng, also an old and seasoned scholar.
translations.idiomatic: The top-ranked graduate that year was Wen Zhenmeng, likewise a mature scholar of long standing.

sentences.zh: 海內鹹慶得人。

translations.literal: Within the seas all rejoiced that worthy men had been obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars throughout the empire celebrated that the examinations had produced men of genuine talent.

sentences.zh: 明年丁內艱，廬墓次。

translations.literal: The next year he mourned inner bereavement, dwelling at the tomb-side.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when his mother died, he took up mourning residence at her tomb.

sentences.zh: 服闋，起故官，尋直經筵，典誥敕。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, recalled to former office; soon attending the Classics Lectern, in charge of edicts and imperial orders.
