translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was recalled to his former post, soon joined the Classics Lectern, and took charge of drafting edicts and rescripts.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢冒邊功，矯旨錫上公爵，給世券。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian falsely claimed border merit; by forged edict enfeoffed the sovereign duke rank, granted hereditary patent.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian fabricated military merit on the frontier and, by forged imperial order, had himself ennobled as a duke and granted a hereditary patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 仁錫當視草，持不可，其黨以威劫之，毅然曰：「世自有視草者，何必我！」

translations.literal: Renxi was to draft the text, held that it could not be; his faction by intimidation coerced him; he resolutely said: 「The world naturally has those who draft imperial texts—why must it be I!
translations.idiomatic: When Renxi was assigned to draft the decree he refused. Wei's faction tried to intimidate him, but he declared firmly: 「There are plenty of people in this world willing to draft edicts for you—why must it be me!

sentences.zh: 忠賢聞之怒。

translations.literal: 」Zhongxian heard and was angry.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian was enraged when he heard of this.

sentences.zh: 不數日，裏人孫文豸以誦《步天歌》見捕，坐妖言鍛煉成獄，詞連仁錫及震孟，罪將不測。

translations.literal: Within not many days, fellow townsmen Sun Wenzhi, for reciting the 《Song of Pacing the Heavens》, was arrested; sat convicted of heterodox speech, forged and refined into a case; the testimony linked Renxi and Zhenmeng; their crimes would be unforeseeable.
translations.idiomatic: Within days a townsman named Sun Wenzhi was arrested for reciting the 《Song of Pacing the Heavens》; framed for seditious speech and tortured into a case, his testimony implicated Renxi and Wen Zhenmeng, and their fates hung in the balance.

sentences.zh: 有密救者，得削籍歸。

translations.literal: There was one who secretly rescued them; they were able to be struck from the register and return.
translations.idiomatic: Through secret intervention they were spared and allowed to return home stripped of office.

sentences.zh: 崇禎改元，召復故官。

translations.literal: When Chongzhen changed the era title, they were summoned to restore former offices.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen reign began he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 旋進右中允，署國子司業事，再直經筵。

translations.literal: Soon promoted to Right Attendant-in-Waiting, acting National University Vice Director affairs, again attending the Classics Lectern.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Right Attendant-in-Waiting, given acting charge of the Vice Directorship of the National University, and again joined the Classics Lectern.

sentences.zh: 以預修神、光二朝實錄，進右諭德，乞假歸。

translations.literal: For participating in compiling the Veritable Records of the Shen and Guang reigns, promoted to Right Junior Mentor; requested leave and returned.
translations.idiomatic: For helping compile the Veritable Records of the Wanli and Taichang reigns he was promoted to Right Junior Mentor, then requested leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 越三年，即家起南京國子祭酒，甫拜命，得疾卒。

translations.literal: After three years, from home summoned to Nanjing National University Chancellor; just upon receiving the appointment, fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he was summoned from home to serve as Chancellor of the Nanjing National University, but fell ill and died soon after accepting the appointment.

sentences.zh: 福王時，贈詹事，謚文莊。

translations.literal: In the Fu Prince's time, posthumously granted Vice Director; posthumous title Wenzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Hanlin Academy and given the temple name Wenzhuang (Cultivated and Dignified).

sentences.zh: 仁錫講求經濟，有誌天下事，性好學，喜著書，一時館閣中博洽者鮮其儔雲。

translations.literal: Renxi pursued statecraft; had ambition for affairs under heaven; by nature loved learning, delighted in composing books—at the time among the Academy and court, broadly learned ones who could match him were few indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Renxi devoted himself to practical statecraft and cared deeply about the affairs of the realm. Naturally studious and fond of writing, among contemporary court scholars few could rival his breadth of learning.

sentences.zh: 董其昌，字玄宰，松江華亭人。

translations.literal: Dong Qichang, styled Xuanzai, was a native of Huating in Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Qichang, styled Xuanzai, was a native of Huating in Songjiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舉萬歷十七年進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Wanli entered as jinshi, transferred to Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the seventeenth year of Wanli and was appointed a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 禮部侍郎田一俊以教習卒官，其昌請假，走數千里，護其喪歸葬。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Rites Tian Yijun died in office while instructing; Qichang requested leave, ran several thousand li, escorted his coffin home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Minister of Rites Tian Yijun died in office while serving as an instructor, Qichang took leave and traveled thousands of miles to escort his coffin home for burial.

sentences.zh: 遷授編修。

translations.literal: Transferred and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was subsequently appointed Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 皇長子出閣，充講官，因事啟沃，皇長子每目屬之。

translations.literal: When the crown prince left the inner quarters, [Dong Qichang] filled the role of lecturer; on various occasions he offered opening counsel, and the crown prince each time fixed his eyes on him.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir apparent left the palace to establish his household, Dong Qichang served as his lecturer; on many occasions he offered candid counsel, and the crown prince would invariably fix his gaze on him.

sentences.zh: 坐失執政意，出為湖廣副使，移疾歸。

translations.literal: Having fallen short of those in power's intent, he was sent out as Huguang Vice Commissioner; he claimed illness and returned.
translations.idiomatic: For falling out of favor with those in power, he was posted out as vice commissioner of Huguang; he pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 起故官，督湖廣學政，不徇請囑，為勢家所怨，嗾生儒數百人鼓噪，毀其公署。

translations.literal: Raised to his former office, he supervised Huguang education; he did not bend to entreaties and patronage, was resented by powerful families, [who] incited several hundred examination candidates to drum and clamor, destroying his public office.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to his former post, he oversaw Huguang provincial education; he refused to yield to solicited favors, and powerful families resented him—they incited several hundred scholar-students to raise a clamor and demolish his official residence.

sentences.zh: 其昌即拜疏求去，帝不許，而令所司按治，其昌卒謝事歸。

translations.literal: Qichang at once submitted a memorial requesting departure; the emperor did not allow it, but ordered the office to investigate and punish; Qichang finally resigned his post and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Qichang immediately submitted a memorial requesting leave; the emperor refused, but ordered the relevant office to investigate; Qichang ultimately resigned his duties and returned home.

sentences.zh: 起山東副使、登萊兵備、河南參政，並不赴。

translations.literal: Raised as Shandong Vice Commissioner, Denglai military intendant, and Henan Administrative Commissioner—in every case he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Shandong vice commissioner, Denglai military intendant, and Henan administrative commissioner—in every case he declined to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 光宗立，問：「舊講官董先生安在？」

translations.literal: Guangzong was established and asked: 「Where is the former lecturer, Master Dong?
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong ascended the throne, he asked, "Where is the former lecturer, Master Dong?"

sentences.zh: 乃召為太常少卿，掌國子司業事。

translations.literal: 」Thereupon [Dong] was summoned as Vice Minister of the Directorate of Ceremonies, managing the affairs of Vice Director of Education in the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Dong was summoned as vice minister of the Directorate of Ceremonies, in charge of the affairs of vice director of education in the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年擢本寺卿，兼侍讀學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he was promoted to Director of his directorate, concurrently serving as Lecturer-in-Waiting in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Tianqi reign he was promoted to director of his directorate and concurrently appointed lecturer-in-waiting in the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 時修《神宗實錄》，命往南方采輯先朝章疏及遺事，其昌慶搜博征，錄成三百本。

translations.literal: At the time they were compiling the 《Veritable Records of Emperor Shenzong》, and he was ordered to go south to collect and compile memorials and anecdotes of the previous reign; Qichang rejoiced in wide searching and broad gathering, recording three hundred volumes.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court was compiling the 《Veritable Records of Emperor Shenzong》; he was ordered to travel south to collect memorials and anecdotes from the previous reign. Qichang searched widely with evident delight and compiled three hundred volumes.

sentences.zh: 又采留中之疏切於國本、藩封、人才、風俗、河渠、食貨、吏治、邊防者，別為四十卷。

translations.literal: He also collected memorials held back at court that bore on the foundation of the state, enfeoffment of princes, talent, customs, waterways, food and goods, governance of officials, and frontier defense, arranging them separately into forty volumes.
translations.idiomatic: He also gathered memorials held back at court that bore on the foundation of the state, enfeoffment of princes, talent, customs, waterways, food and goods, governance of officials, and frontier defense, arranging them separately into forty volumes.

sentences.zh: 仿史贊之例，每篇系以筆斷。

translations.literal: Following the example of historical commentaries, to each piece he attached a brush judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Following the example of historical commentaries, he appended to each piece his own judgment in brush.

sentences.zh: 書成表進，有詔褒美，宣付史館。

translations.literal: When the work was finished he submitted it by memorial; there was an edict praising him, and it was ordered sent to the Historical Archives.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished he submitted it by memorial; an edict praised him, and the compilation was ordered sent to the Historical Archives.

sentences.zh: 明年秋，擢禮部右侍郎，協理詹事府事，尋轉左侍郎。

translations.literal: The next autumn he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Rites and Assistant Director of the Crown Prince's Household; soon after he was transferred to Left Vice Minister.
translations.idiomatic: The following autumn he was promoted to right vice minister of rites and assistant director of the Crown Prince's Household; soon after he was transferred to left vice minister.

sentences.zh: 五年正月拜南京禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year he was appointed Minister of Rites at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year of Tianqi he was appointed minister of rites at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 時政在奄豎，黨禍酷烈。

translations.literal: At the time political power lay with eunuch attendants, and factional persecution was fierce.
translations.idiomatic: At the time power lay with the eunuchs, and factional persecution was fierce.

sentences.zh: 其昌深自引遠，逾年請告歸。

translations.literal: Qichang kept himself deeply aloof; after more than a year he requested leave and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Qichang kept himself deeply aloof; after more than a year he requested leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年起故官，掌詹事府事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he was raised to his former office and put in charge of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he was recalled to his former post and put in charge of the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 居三年，屢疏乞休，詔加太子太保致仕。

translations.literal: After three years in office he repeatedly submitted memorials begging to retire; an edict added the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted retirement.
translations.idiomatic: After three years he repeatedly submitted memorials begging to retire; an edict added the title grand guardian of the heir apparent and granted him retirement.

sentences.zh: 又二年卒，年八十有三。

translations.literal: Two years later he died, at the age of eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he died, at the age of eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太傅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the title Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the title grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 福王時，謚文敏。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu, he was given the posthumous name Wenmin.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was given the posthumous name Wenmin.

sentences.zh: 其昌天才俊逸，少負重名。

translations.literal: Qichang was gifted with extraordinary talent; from youth he bore a heavy reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Qichang was gifted with extraordinary talent; from youth he bore a great reputation.

sentences.zh: 初，華亭自沈度、沈粲以後，南安知府張弼、詹事陸深、布政莫如忠及子是龍皆以善書稱。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Huating since Shen Du and Shen Can, the prefect of Nan'an Zhang Bi, Junior Mentor Lu Shen, Provincial Administration Commissioner Mo Ruzhong, and his son Shi Long were all acclaimed for skill in calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in Huating since Shen Du and Shen Can, the prefect of Nan'an Zhang Bi, junior mentor Lu Shen, provincial administration commissioner Mo Ruzhong, and Mo's son Shi Long had all been acclaimed for skill in calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 其昌後出，超越諸家，始以宋米芾為宗。

translations.literal: Qichang came later and surpassed all the schools, initially taking the Song calligrapher Mi Fu as his master.
translations.idiomatic: Qichang came later and surpassed all the schools, initially taking the Song calligrapher Mi Fu as his model.

sentences.zh: 後自成一家，名聞外國。

translations.literal: Later he formed a school of his own, and his name was heard in foreign lands.
translations.idiomatic: Later he formed a school of his own, and his fame spread even beyond the realm.

sentences.zh: 其畫集宋、元諸家之長，行以己意，瀟灑生動，非人力所及也。

translations.literal: His painting gathered the strengths of Song and Yuan masters, executed with his own intent—effortless and vivid, beyond what human effort could reach.
translations.idiomatic: His painting gathered the strengths of Song and Yuan masters, executed with his own intent—effortless and vivid, beyond what human effort could achieve.

sentences.zh: 四方金石之刻，得其制作手書，以為二絕。

translations.literal: For stone inscriptions throughout the realm, to obtain both his design and his own hand in writing was regarded as a double perfection.
translations.idiomatic: For stone inscriptions throughout the realm, to obtain both his design and his own hand in writing was regarded as a double perfection.

sentences.zh: 造請無虛日，尺素短劄，流布人間，爭購寶之。

translations.literal: Visitors came without a day free; letters and brief notes circulated among the people, and all competed to purchase and treasure them.
translations.idiomatic: Visitors came without a day free; letters and brief notes circulated among the people, and all competed to purchase and treasure them.

sentences.zh: 精於品題，收藏家得片語只字以為重。

translations.literal: He was skilled at connoisseurship; collectors prized even a phrase or a single character from him.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at connoisseurship; collectors prized even a phrase or a single character from him.

sentences.zh: 性和易，通禪理，蕭閑吐納，終日無俗語。

translations.literal: His nature was easygoing; he mastered Chan Buddhist principles, and in quiet ease practiced breath control—throughout the day no vulgar speech.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was easygoing; he mastered Chan Buddhist principles, and in quiet ease practiced breath control—throughout the day he spoke no vulgar words.

sentences.zh: 人儗之米芾、趙孟頫雲。

translations.literal: People compared him to Mi Fu and Zhao Mengfu, they say.
translations.idiomatic: People compared him to Mi Fu and Zhao Mengfu.

sentences.zh: 同時以善書名者，臨邑刑侗、順天米萬鐘、晉江張瑞圖，時人謂刑、張、米、董，又曰南董、北米。

translations.literal: Those famed at the same time for calligraphy were Linyi Xing Tong, Shuntian Mi Wanzhong, and Jinjiang Zhang Ruitu; contemporaries called them Xing, Zhang, Mi, and Dong, or again "Dong in the south, Mi in the north."
translations.idiomatic: Those famed at the same time for calligraphy were Linyi's Xing Tong, Shuntian's Mi Wanzhong, and Jinjiang's Zhang Ruitu; contemporaries called them Xing, Zhang, Mi, and Dong, or again "Dong in the south, Mi in the north."

sentences.zh: 然三人者，不逮其昌遠甚。

translations.literal: Yet the three of them fell far short of Qichang.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the three of them fell far short of Qichang.

sentences.zh: 莫如忠，字子良。

translations.literal: Mo Ruzhong, courtesy name Ziliang.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Ruzhong, courtesy name Ziliang.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十七年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the seventeenth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the seventeenth year of the Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 累官浙江布政使。

translations.literal: Through successive offices he rose to Provincial Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive offices to provincial administration commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 潔修自好。

translations.literal: He cultivated purity and kept himself chaste.
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated purity and kept himself above reproach.

sentences.zh: 夏言死，經紀其喪。

translations.literal: When Xia Yan died, he managed his funeral arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia Yan died, he managed his funeral arrangements.

sentences.zh: 善草書，詩文有體要。

translations.literal: He was skilled at cursive script; his poetry and prose had structure and principle.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at cursive script; his poetry and prose had structure and substance.

sentences.zh: 是龍，字雲卿，後以字行，更字廷韓。

translations.literal: Shi Long, courtesy name Yunqing; later he was known by his courtesy name and changed his style name to Tinghan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Long, courtesy name Yunqing; later he was known by his courtesy name and changed his style name to Tinghan.

sentences.zh: 十歲能文，長善書。

translations.literal: At ten he could compose essays; as an adult he excelled at calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he could compose essays; as an adult he excelled at calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 皇甫汸、王世貞輩亟稱之。

translations.literal: Huangfu Fan, Wang Shizhen, and their circle praised him repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Fan, Wang Shizhen, and their circle praised him highly.

sentences.zh: 以貢生終。

translations.literal: He ended his career as a tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as a tribute student.

sentences.zh: 刑侗，字子願。

translations.literal: Xing Tong, courtesy name Ziyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Tong, courtesy name Ziyuan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the second year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 終陜西行太仆卿。

translations.literal: He ended as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 家資鉅萬，築來禽館於古犁丘，減產奉客，遂致中落。

translations.literal: His family wealth was vast—in the tens of thousands; he built the Coming-Birds Pavilion at ancient Liqiu, reduced his estate to entertain guests, and so fell into moderate ruin.
translations.idiomatic: His family wealth ran to tens of thousands; he built the Coming-Birds Pavilion at ancient Liqiu, reduced his estate to entertain guests, and so fell into moderate ruin.

sentences.zh: 妹慈靜，善仿兄書。

translations.literal: His younger sister Cijing was skilled at imitating her brother's calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: His younger sister Cijing was skilled at imitating her brother's calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 米萬鐘，字友石。

translations.literal: Mi Wanzhong, courtesy name Youshi.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Wanzhong, courtesy name Youshi.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十三年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the twenty-third year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-third year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 歷官江西按察使。

translations.literal: Through successive offices he rose to Surveillance Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive offices to surveillance commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年，魏忠賢黨倪文煥劾之，遂削籍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianqi, Ni Wenhuan, a partisan of Wei Zhongxian, impeached him, and he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tianqi, Ni Wenhuan, a partisan of Wei Zhongxian, impeached him, and he was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，起太仆少卿，卒官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he was raised as Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign he was recalled as vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and died in office.

sentences.zh: 張瑞圖者，官至大學士，逆案中人也。

translations.literal: As for Zhang Ruitu, he rose to Grand Secretary and was a man implicated in the factional cases.
translations.idiomatic: As for Zhang Ruitu, he rose to grand secretary and was a man implicated in the eunuch faction cases.

sentences.zh: 袁宏道，字中郎，公安人。

translations.literal: Yuan Hongdao, courtesy name Zhonglang, a native of Gong'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hongdao, courtesy name Zhonglang, was a native of Gong'an.

sentences.zh: 與兄宗道、弟中道並有才名，時稱「三袁」。

translations.literal: Together with his elder brother Zongdao and younger brother Zhongdao he all had literary fame; at the time they were called 「the Three Yuans.」
translations.idiomatic: Together with his elder brother Zongdao and younger brother Zhongdao he shared literary fame; at the time they were called "the Three Yuans."

sentences.zh: 宗道，字伯修。

translations.literal: Zongdao, courtesy name Boxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zongdao, courtesy name Boxiu.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十四年會試第一。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Wanli he placed first in the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Wanli he placed first in the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 授庶吉士，進編修，卒官右庶子。

translations.literal: Appointed as Hanlin bachelor, he advanced to compiler, and died in office as Right Subdirector of the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Hanlin bachelor, he advanced to compiler and died in office as right subdirector of the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 泰昌時，追錄光宗講官，贈禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Taichang reign he was posthumously recorded among Guangzong's lecturers and granted the posthumous office of Right Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taichang reign he was posthumously recorded among Guangzong's lecturers and granted the posthumous office of right vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 宏道年十六為諸生，即結社城南，為之長。

translations.literal: Hongdao at sixteen became a registered student and immediately formed a literary society south of the city, serving as its head.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen Hongdao became a registered student and immediately formed a literary society south of the city, serving as its head.

sentences.zh: 閑為詩歌古文，有聲里中。

translations.literal: In his leisure he wrote poetry and ancient-style prose, and had a reputation in the district.
translations.idiomatic: In his leisure he wrote poetry and ancient-style prose and gained a reputation in the district.

sentences.zh: 舉萬歷二十年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the twentieth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twentieth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 歸家，下帷讀書，詩文主妙悟。

translations.literal: Returning home, he lowered the curtain and read; in poetry and prose he advocated subtle awakening.
translations.idiomatic: Returning home, he lowered the curtain and devoted himself to reading; in poetry and prose he advocated intuitive insight.

sentences.zh: 選吳縣知縣，聽斷敏決，公庭鮮事。

translations.literal: Selected as magistrate of Wuxian, he judged cases with swift decisiveness, and there were few matters in the public hall.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as magistrate of Wuxian, he judged cases with swift decisiveness, and there were few matters pending in the public hall.

sentences.zh: 與士大夫談說詩文，以風雅自命。

translations.literal: With literati he discoursed on poetry and prose, styling himself a man of elegant taste.
translations.idiomatic: With literati he discoursed on poetry and prose, styling himself a man of refined taste.

sentences.zh: 已而解官去。

translations.literal: Soon he resigned his office and left.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he resigned his office and left.

sentences.zh: 起授順天教授，歷國子助教、禮部主事，謝病歸。

translations.literal: Raised and appointed professor in Shuntian, he served successively as tutor in the Imperial Academy and Director in the Ministry of Rites; he pleaded illness and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled, he was appointed professor in Shuntian, then served successively as tutor in the Imperial Academy and director in the Ministry of Rites; he pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 久之，起故官。

translations.literal: After a long time he was raised to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 尋以清望擢吏部驗封主事，改文選。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of his standing for integrity, he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel for the Verification and Sealing Section, then transferred to the Selection Section.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, on account of his reputation for integrity, he was promoted to director in the Ministry of Personnel for the verification and sealing section, then transferred to the selection section.

sentences.zh: 尋移考功員外郎，立歲終考察群吏法，言：「外官三歲一察，京官六歲，武官五歲，此曹安得獨免？」

translations.literal: Soon transferred to Assistant Director in the Ministry of Personnel for merit evaluation, he established the law for year-end review of all officials, stating: 「Outside officials are inspected once every three years, capital officials every six years, military officials every five years—how can this lot alone be exempt?
translations.idiomatic: Soon transferred to assistant director in the Ministry of Personnel for merit evaluation, he established the law for year-end review of all officials, stating, "Outside officials are inspected once every three years, capital officials every six years, military officials every five years—how can this group alone be exempt?"

sentences.zh: 疏上，報可，遂為定制。

translations.literal: 」When the memorial was submitted, approval was granted, and it became fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, approval was granted, and it became fixed regulation.

sentences.zh: 遷稽勛郎中，後謝病歸，數月卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel for meritorious deeds; later he pleaded illness and returned home, and died several months later.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director in the Ministry of Personnel for meritorious deeds; later he pleaded illness and returned home, and died several months later.

sentences.zh: 中道，字小修。

translations.literal: Zhongdao, courtesy name Xiaoxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongdao, courtesy name Xiaoxiu.

sentences.zh: 十余歲，作《黃山》、《雪》二賦，五千余言。

translations.literal: Before he was ten he wrote the two fu 《Mount Huang》 and 《Snow》, more than five thousand characters in all.
translations.idiomatic: Before he was ten he wrote the two fu 《Mount Huang》 and 《Snow》, more than five thousand characters in all.

sentences.zh: 長益豪邁，從兩兄宦遊京師，多交四方名士，足跡半天下。

translations.literal: As he grew he became even more bold and free; following his two elder brothers on official tours to the capital, he made many acquaintances among famous men throughout the realm, and his footsteps covered half the world.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew he became even more bold and free; following his two elder brothers on official tours to the capital, he made many acquaintances among famous men throughout the realm, and his footsteps covered half the world.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十一年始舉於鄉。

translations.literal: Not until the thirty-first year of Wanli did he pass the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the thirty-first year of Wanli did he pass the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 又十四年乃成進士。

translations.literal: Fourteen years more passed before he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen years more passed before he became a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 由徽州教授，歷國子博士、南京禮部主事。

translations.literal: Starting as professor in Huizhou, he served successively as doctorate in the Imperial Academy and Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Starting as professor in Huizhou, he served successively as doctorate in the Imperial Academy and director in the Nanjing Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 天啟四年進南京吏部郎中，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianqi he was promoted to Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Tianqi he was promoted to director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue and died in office.

sentences.zh: 先是，王、李之學盛行，袁氏兄弟獨心非之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Wang and Li school flourished widely; the Yuan brothers alone inwardly disapproved of it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Wang and Li school flourished widely; the Yuan brothers alone inwardly disapproved of it.

sentences.zh: 宗道在館中，與同館黃輝力排其說。

translations.literal: Zongdao, while in the Hanlin Academy, together with his colleague Huang Hui strongly opposed their doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: While in the Hanlin Academy, Zongdao together with his colleague Huang Hui strongly opposed their doctrine.

sentences.zh: 於唐好白樂天，於宋好蘇軾，名其齋曰白蘇。

translations.literal: In the Tang he favored Bai Juyi; in the Song he favored Su Shi; he named his studio White-Su.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tang he favored Bai Juyi; in the Song he favored Su Shi; he named his studio White-Su.

sentences.zh: 至宏道，益矯以清新輕俊，學者多舍王、李而從之，目為公安體。

translations.literal: By the time of Hongdao, he further overcorrected toward freshness, clarity, lightness, and wit; many students abandoned Wang and Li and followed him, calling it the Gong'an style.
translations.idiomatic: By Hongdao's time the movement overcorrected further toward freshness, clarity, lightness, and wit; many students abandoned Wang and Li and followed him, calling it the Gong'an style.

sentences.zh: 然戲謔嘲笑，間雜俚語，空疏者便之。

translations.literal: Yet with jesting ridicule mixed in and vulgar speech at times, those shallow of learning found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Yet with jesting ridicule mixed in and vulgar speech at times, those shallow of learning found it convenient.

sentences.zh: 其後，王、李風漸息，而鐘、譚之說大熾。

translations.literal: Afterward the Wang and Li vogue gradually faded, while the doctrines of Zhong and Tan blazed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the Wang and Li vogue gradually faded, while the doctrines of Zhong and Tan blazed greatly.

sentences.zh: 鐘、譚者，鐘惺、譚元春也。

translations.literal: Zhong and Tan—that is, Zhong Xing and Tan Yuanchun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong and Tan—that is, Zhong Xing and Tan Yuanchun.

sentences.zh: 惺，字伯敬，竟陵人。

translations.literal: Xing, courtesy name Bojing, a native of Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: Xing, courtesy name Bojing, was a native of Jingling.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十八年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the thirty-eighth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-eighth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授行人，稍遷工部主事，尋改南京禮部，進郎中。

translations.literal: Appointed as Traveling Censor, he was gradually promoted to Director in the Ministry of Works, then transferred to the Nanjing Ministry of Rites and advanced to Director.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed traveling censor, he was gradually promoted to director in the Ministry of Works, then transferred to the Nanjing Ministry of Rites and advanced to director.

sentences.zh: 擢福建提學僉事，以父憂歸，卒於家。

translations.literal: Promoted to Education Intendant of Fujian, he returned home on account of mourning for his father and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to education intendant of Fujian, he returned home to mourn his father and died there.

sentences.zh: 惺貌寢，羸不勝衣，為人嚴冷，不喜接俗客，由此得謝人事。

translations.literal: Xing's appearance was unprepossessing; he was frail and barely filled his clothes. In conduct he was stern and cold, disliking to receive vulgar guests—thereby he gained release from worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Xing's appearance was unprepossessing; he was frail and barely filled his clothes. In conduct he was stern and cold and disliked receiving vulgar guests—thereby he gained release from worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 官南都，僦秦淮水閣讀史，恒至丙夜，有所見即筆之，名曰《史懷》。

translations.literal: While serving in the southern capital he rented a waterside pavilion on the Qinhuai to read history, often until the third watch of the night; whatever he observed he wrote down at once, calling it 《Reflections on History》.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the southern capital he rented a waterside pavilion on the Qinhuai to read history, often until the third watch of the night; whatever he observed he wrote down at once, calling it 《Reflections on History》.

sentences.zh: 晚逃於禪以卒。

translations.literal: In his later years he took refuge in Chan Buddhism until death.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he took refuge in Chan Buddhism until his death.

sentences.zh: 自宏道矯王、李詩之弊，倡以清真，惺復矯其弊，變而為幽深孤峭。

translations.literal: After Hongdao had overcorrected the defects of Wang and Li poetry by advocating purity and truth, Xing again overcorrected those defects, changing into depth, remoteness, solitude, and austerity.
translations.idiomatic: After Hongdao had overcorrected the defects of Wang and Li poetry by advocating purity and truth, Xing again overcorrected those defects, changing the style into depth, remoteness, solitude, and austerity.

sentences.zh: 與同里譚元春評選唐人之詩為《唐詩歸》，又評選隋以前詩為《古詩歸》。

translations.literal: Together with his fellow townsman Tan Yuanchun he selected and appraised Tang poetry as 《Return to Tang Poetry》, and also selected pre-Sui poetry as 《Return to Ancient Poetry》.
translations.idiomatic: Together with his fellow townsman Tan Yuanchun he selected and appraised Tang poetry as 《Return to Tang Poetry》, and also selected pre-Sui poetry as 《Return to Ancient Poetry》.

sentences.zh: 鐘、譚之名滿天下，謂之竟陵體。

translations.literal: The names of Zhong and Tan filled the world; this was called the Jingling style.
translations.idiomatic: The names of Zhong and Tan filled the world; this was called the Jingling style.

sentences.zh: 然兩人學不甚富，其識解多僻，大為通人所譏。

translations.literal: Yet the learning of the two men was not very rich; their interpretations were often eccentric, and they were greatly ridiculed by those broadly learned.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the learning of the two men was not very rich; their interpretations were often eccentric, and they were greatly ridiculed by the broadly learned.

sentences.zh: 元春，字友夏，名輩後於惺，以《詩歸》故，與齊名。

translations.literal: Yuanchun, courtesy name Youxia; though junior in reputation to Xing, because of the 《Poetry Returns》 he was ranked equally with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanchun, courtesy name Youxia; though junior in reputation to Xing, because of the 《Poetry Returns》 he was ranked equally with him.

sentences.zh: 至天啟七年始舉鄉試第一，惺已前卒矣。

translations.literal: Not until the seventh year of Tianqi did he place first in the provincial examination—by then Xing had already died earlier.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the seventh year of Tianqi did he place first in the provincial examination—by then Xing had already died.

sentences.zh: 王惟儉，字損仲，祥符人。

translations.literal: Wang Weijian, courtesy name Sunzhong, was a native of Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Weijian, courtesy name Sunzhong, was from Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十三年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-third year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授濰縣知縣，遷兵部職方主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Weixian County, then transferred to be a secretary in the Bureau of Operations of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Weixian County and later promoted to secretary in the Ministry of War's Bureau of Operations.

sentences.zh: 三十年春，遼東總兵官馬林以忤稅使高淮被逮，兵部尚書田樂等救之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirtieth year, Ma Lin, regional commander of Liaodong, was arrested for offending the tax commissioner Gao Huai; Minister of War Tian Le and others came to his rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirtieth year of Wanli, Ma Lin, the regional commander of Liaodong, was arrested after offending the tax commissioner Gao Huai; Minister of War Tian Le and others intervened on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，責職方不推代者，空司而逐，惟儉亦削籍歸。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and blamed the Bureau of Operations for not recommending replacements; he emptied the bureau and dismissed its staff, and Weijian too was struck from the registers and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and blamed the Bureau of Operations for failing to recommend successors; he emptied the bureau and dismissed its entire staff, and Weijian was also struck from the official rolls and sent home.

sentences.zh: 家居二十年，光宗立，起光祿丞。

translations.literal: He lived at home for twenty years; when Emperor Guangzong ascended the throne, he was recalled as Commissioner of the Imperial Household Department for Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He remained at home for twenty years until Emperor Guangzong took the throne, when he was recalled to serve as Commissioner of the Imperial Household Department for Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 三遷大理少卿。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted three times to Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 天啟三年八月擢右僉都御史，巡撫山東。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Tianqi he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and appointed Grand Coordinator of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year of Tianqi he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and made Grand Coordinator of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 值徐鴻儒之亂，民多逃亡，遼人避難來者，亦多失所，惟儉加意綏輯。

translations.literal: It happened during the rebellion of Xu Hongru; many common people fled, and many Liaodong refugees who came seeking safety also lost their homes and livelihoods—Weijian gave special attention to pacifying and organizing them.
translations.idiomatic: During Xu Hongru's rebellion, many people fled, and Liaodong refugees who came seeking safety often found themselves destitute; Weijian devoted special care to pacifying and resettling them.

sentences.zh: 五年三月擢南京兵部右侍郎，未赴。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of War at Nanjing, but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of War at Nanjing, but never assumed the office.

sentences.zh: 入為工部右侍郎，魏忠賢黨御史田景新劾之，落職閑住。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Right Vice Minister of Works; the censor Tian Jingxin, a follower of Wei Zhongxian, impeached him, and he was dismissed from office and lived in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the capital as Right Vice Minister of Works, but the censor Tian Jingxin, a follower of Wei Zhongxian, impeached him, and he was dismissed and forced into retirement.

sentences.zh: 惟儉資敏嗜學。

translations.literal: Weijian was naturally quick and loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: Weijian was quick-witted and devoted to learning.

sentences.zh: 初被廢，肆力經史百家。

translations.literal: When he was first dismissed from office, he applied himself with full force to the classics, histories, and the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: After his first dismissal from office, he devoted himself wholeheartedly to the classics, histories, and the hundred schools of thought.

sentences.zh: 苦《宋史》繁蕪，手刪定，自為一書。

translations.literal: Finding the 《History of Song》 excessively cumbersome, he edited it by hand and made it into a book of his own.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the 《History of Song》 excessively cumbersome, he edited it by hand into a work of his own.

sentences.zh: 好書畫古玩。

translations.literal: He loved calligraphy, painting, and antique curios.
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of calligraphy, painting, and antique curios.

sentences.zh: 萬歷、天啟間，世所稱博物君子，惟儉與董其昌並，而嘉興李日華亞之。

translations.literal: During the Wanli and Tianqi reigns, among the broadly learned gentlemen praised by the age, Weijian stood equal with Dong Qichang, while Li Rihua of Jiaxing ranked just below them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli and Tianqi reigns, among the broadly learned gentlemen celebrated by the age, Weijian was ranked alongside Dong Qichang, with Li Rihua of Jiaxing just below them.

sentences.zh: 日華，字君實，嘉興人。

translations.literal: Rihua, courtesy name Junshi, was a native of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rihua, courtesy name Junshi, was from Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十年進士。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twentieth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 官至太仆少卿。

translations.literal: His highest office was Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 恬淡和易，與物無忤。

translations.literal: He was calm, easygoing, and at peace with everyone.
translations.idiomatic: He was calm and easygoing and never at odds with anyone.

sentences.zh: 惟儉則口多微詞，好抨擊道學，人不能堪。

translations.literal: Weijian, by contrast, often spoke with subtle barbs and loved to attack Neo-Confucian moralism—people could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Weijian, by contrast, was given to subtle sarcasm and loved attacking Neo-Confucian moralism, which people found hard to tolerate.

sentences.zh: 嘗與時輩宴集，征《漢書》一事，具悉本末，指其腹笑曰：「名下寧有虛士乎！」

translations.literal: Once at a banquet with contemporaries, when a matter from the 《Book of Han》 was raised, he knew the whole story from beginning to end; pointing to his belly he laughed and said: 「Can there be an empty scholar beneath so great a name!」
translations.idiomatic: Once at a gathering with contemporaries, when a question from the 《Book of Han》 was raised, he knew the whole story from beginning to end; patting his belly he laughed and said, 「Can a man of such renown be an empty scholar!」

sentences.zh: 其自喜如此。

translations.literal: 」Such was his self-satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the pleasure he took in himself.

sentences.zh: 曹學佺，字能始，侯官人。

translations.literal: Cao Xuequan, courtesy name Nengshi, was a native of Houguan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xuequan, courtesy name Nengshi, was from Houguan.

sentences.zh: 弱冠舉萬歷二十三年進士，授戶部主事。

translations.literal: At the age of capping he passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-third year of Wanli and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-third year of Wanli and was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 中察典，調南京添註大理左寺正。

translations.literal: He failed the inspection review and was transferred to Nanjing as a supplementary appointee as Left Assistant Director of the Grand Court of Revision.
translations.idiomatic: After failing the inspection review, he was transferred to Nanjing as supplementary Left Assistant Director of the Grand Court of Revision.

sentences.zh: 居冗散七年，肆力於學。

translations.literal: He spent seven years in a supernumerary and idle post, applying himself with full force to learning.
translations.idiomatic: He spent seven years in a supernumerary post with little to do, devoting himself wholeheartedly to study.

sentences.zh: 累遷南京戶部郎中，四川右參政、按察使。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he became a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue, then Right Assistant Administration Commissioner and Surveillance Commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in turn to director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue, then to Right Assistant Administration Commissioner and Surveillance Commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 蜀府毀於火，估修資七十萬金，學牷以《宗藩條例》卻之。

translations.literal: The princely residence in Shu was destroyed by fire; the estimated repair cost was seven hundred thousand taels of silver; Xuequan rejected it on the basis of the 《Regulations for Imperial Clans》.
translations.idiomatic: When the princely residence in Shu was destroyed by fire, the estimated repair cost came to seven hundred thousand taels of silver; Xuequan rejected the expense under the 《Regulations for Imperial Clans》.

sentences.zh: 又中察典，議調。

translations.literal: He again failed the inspection review, and a transfer was proposed.
translations.idiomatic: He failed the inspection review again, and a transfer was proposed.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年起廣西右參議。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he was recalled as Right Administration Vice Commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianqi he was recalled to serve as Right Administration Vice Commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 初，梃擊獄興，劉廷元輩主瘋顛。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Killing-with-a-Staff case arose, Liu Tingyuan and his faction maintained that the assailant had been insane.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Killing-with-a-Staff case broke, Liu Tingyuan and his allies argued that the assailant had been insane.

sentences.zh: 學牷著《野史紀略》，直書事本末。

translations.literal: Xuequan wrote the 《Outline of Unofficial History》, recording the events straightforwardly from beginning to end.
translations.idiomatic: Xuequan wrote the 《Outline of Unofficial History》, setting down the events plainly from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 至六年秋，學牷遷陜西副使，未行，而廷元附魏忠賢大幸，乃劾學牷私撰野史，淆亂國章，遂削籍，毀所鏤板。

translations.literal: By the autumn of the sixth year Xuequan was transferred to be Vice Commissioner of Shaanxi, but before he departed Tingyuan, now greatly favored through attachment to Wei Zhongxian, impeached Xuequan for privately composing unofficial history and confusing the statutes of the state; Xuequan was struck from the registers and his carved printing blocks were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the sixth year Xuequan was transferred to Vice Commissioner of Shaanxi, but before he could depart, Tingyuan—now greatly favored as a follower of Wei Zhongxian—impeached him for privately writing unofficial history and subverting the statutes of the state; Xuequan was struck from the rolls and his printing blocks were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史王政新，以嘗薦學牷，亦勒閑住。

translations.literal: The touring censor Wang Zhengxin, because he had once recommended Xuequan, was also compelled to retire.
translations.idiomatic: The touring censor Wang Zhengxin, who had once recommended Xuequan, was also forced into retirement.

sentences.zh: 廣西大吏揣學牷必得重禍，羈留以待。

translations.literal: The high officials of Guangxi surmised that Xuequan would surely suffer severe punishment and detained him to wait.
translations.idiomatic: The senior officials of Guangxi assumed Xuequan would face severe punishment and detained him while they waited.

sentences.zh: 已，知忠賢無意殺之，乃得釋還。

translations.literal: Afterward, learning that Zhongxian had no intention of killing him, he was released and allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when it became clear that Zhongxian had no intention of killing him, he was released and allowed to go home.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，起廣西副使，力辭不就。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he was recalled as Vice Commissioner of Guangxi, but firmly declined and did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Chongzhen reign he was recalled as Vice Commissioner of Guangxi, but firmly declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 家居二十年，著書所居石倉園中，為《石倉十二代詩選》，盛行於世。

translations.literal: He lived at home for twenty years, writing books in his Stone Granary Garden; he compiled the 《Stone Granary Anthology of Poetry from Twelve Dynasties》, which circulated widely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home for twenty years, writing in his Stone Granary Garden; his 《Stone Granary Anthology of Poetry from Twelve Dynasties》 became widely popular.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂「二氏有藏，吾儒何獨無」，欲修儒藏與鼎立。

translations.literal: He once said, 「The Two Teachings have their treasuries—why should Confucianism alone have none?」 and wished to compile a Confucian treasury to stand as a third pillar.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, 「Buddhism and Daoism each have their canon—why should Confucianism alone have none?」 and planned to compile a Confucian treasury to stand alongside them.

sentences.zh: 采擷四庫書，因類分輯，十有余年，功未及竣，兩京繼覆。

translations.literal: He gathered and excerpted books from the four repositories and arranged them by category; for more than ten years the work was not yet finished when the two capitals fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years he gathered books from the four repositories and arranged them by category, but the work was still unfinished when both capitals fell in succession.

sentences.zh: 唐王立於閩中，起授太常卿。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Tang established himself in Fujian, Xuequan was recalled and appointed Minister of Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Tang established his court in Fujian, Xuequan was recalled and appointed Minister of Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 尋遷禮部右侍郎兼侍講學士，進尚書，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Right Vice Minister of Rites and Concurrent Lecturing Academician, then promoted to Minister and given the additional title of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Right Vice Minister of Rites and Concurrent Lecturing Academician, then promoted to Minister of Rites with the additional title of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 及事敗，走入山中，投繯而死，年七十有四。

translations.literal: When the cause failed, he fled into the mountains and hanged himself; he was seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: When the cause collapsed, he fled into the mountains and hanged himself at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 詩文甚富，總名《石倉集》。

translations.literal: His poetry and prose were very abundant, gathered under the title 《Collected Works from the Stone Granary》.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and prose were voluminous, collected under the title 《Collected Works from the Stone Granary》.

sentences.zh: 萬歷中，閩中文風頗盛，自學牷倡之，晚年更以殉節著雲。

translations.literal: During Wanli the literary culture of Fujian flourished greatly; Xuequan led the way, and in his later years he became even more renowned for dying for his principles.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign literary culture flourished in Fujian under Xuequan's leadership, and in his later years he became even more celebrated for dying for his principles.

sentences.zh: 其同邑後起者，曾異撰，字弗人，晉江人，家侯官。

translations.literal: Among those who rose later from the same district was Zeng Yizhuan, courtesy name Furen, a native of Jinjiang whose family resided in Houguan.
translations.idiomatic: Among those who rose later from the same district was Zeng Yizhuan, courtesy name Furen, a native of Jinjiang whose family lived in Houguan.

sentences.zh: 父為諸生，早卒。

translations.literal: His father was a licentiate and died early.
translations.idiomatic: His father was a licentiate who died young.

sentences.zh: 母張氏，以遺腹生。

translations.literal: His mother was née Zhang; he was born posthumously.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was née Zhang; he was born after his father's death.

sentences.zh: 家寠甚，紡績給晨夕。

translations.literal: The family was extremely poor; they spun thread to supply morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: The family was desperately poor; they spun thread to keep themselves fed from day to day.

sentences.zh: 異撰起孤童，事母至孝。

translations.literal: Yizhuan grew up as a fatherless child and served his mother with utmost filial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhuan grew up fatherless and served his mother with the utmost filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，采薯葉雜糠乞食之，母妻嘗負畚鋤乾草給爨。

translations.literal: In years of famine they gathered sweet-potato leaves mixed with chaff to beg for food; his mother and wife would carry baskets and hoes to gather dry grass for the cooking fire.
translations.idiomatic: In famine years they gathered sweet-potato leaves mixed with chaff to stave off hunger; his mother and wife would carry baskets and hoes to gather dry grass for fuel.

sentences.zh: 然性介甚，長吏知其貧，欲為地，不屑也。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was extremely upright; when senior officials knew of his poverty and wished to make a place for him, he disdained it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was fiercely upright; when senior officials learned of his poverty and wished to help him along, he refused.

sentences.zh: 吳興潘曾纮督學政，上其母節行，獲旌於朝。

translations.literal: Pan Zenghong of Wuxing, supervising educational policy, reported his mother's chaste conduct, and she received imperial commendation at court.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Zenghong of Wuxing, as provincial education commissioner, reported his mother's chaste conduct, and she received imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 及曾纮巡撫南、贛，得王惟儉所撰《宋史》，招異撰及新建徐世溥更定，未成而罷。

translations.literal: When Zenghong became Grand Coordinator of southern Jiangxi, he obtained Wang Weijian's revised 《History of Song》, summoned Yizhuan and Xu Shipu of Xinjian to revise it further, but the work was unfinished when the project was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Zenghong became Grand Coordinator of southern Jiangxi, he obtained Wang Weijian's revised 《History of Song》 and summoned Yizhuan and Xu Shipu of Xinjian to revise it further, but the project was abandoned before it was finished.

sentences.zh: 異撰久為諸生，究心經世學，所為詩，有奇氣。

translations.literal: Yizhuan long remained a licentiate, devoting himself to statecraft learning; the poetry he wrote had a singular force.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhuan remained a licentiate for many years, devoting himself to statecraft; his poetry had a singular force.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十二年舉鄉試，年四十有九矣，再赴會試還，遂卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Chongzhen he passed the provincial examination at the age of forty-nine; after returning from a second attempt at the metropolitan examination, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Chongzhen he passed the provincial examination at forty-nine; he died shortly after returning from a second attempt at the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 王誌堅，字弱生，昆山人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhijian, courtesy name Ruosheng, was a native of Kunshan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhijian, courtesy name Ruosheng, was from Kunshan.

sentences.zh: 父臨亨，進士。

translations.literal: His father Linheng was a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Linheng was a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 杭州知府。

translations.literal: Prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 誌堅舉萬歷三十八年進士，授南京兵部主事，遷員外郎、郎中。

translations.literal: Zhijian passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-eighth year of Wanli, was appointed a secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of War, and was promoted to vice director and then director.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijian passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-eighth year of Wanli, was appointed a secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of War, and rose to vice director and then director.

sentences.zh: 暇日要同舍郎為讀史社，撰《讀史商語》。

translations.literal: On free days he invited fellow officials to form a History-Reading Society and wrote the 《Historical Discussions》.
translations.idiomatic: In his spare time he gathered fellow officials into a History-Reading Society and wrote the 《Historical Discussions》.

sentences.zh: 遷貴州提學僉事，不赴，乞侍養歸。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Education Intendant of Guizhou, but did not go; he requested leave to return home and care for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Education Intendant of Guizhou but declined the post, requesting leave to return home and care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年起督浙江驛傳，奔母喪歸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he was recalled to supervise postal stations in Zhejiang, then rushed home upon his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianqi he was recalled to supervise postal stations in Zhejiang, but rushed home when his mother died.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年復以僉事督湖廣學政，禮部推為學政第一。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he again served as intendant supervising educational policy in Huguang; the Ministry of Rites ranked him first among education intendants.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Chongzhen he again served as education intendant for Huguang; the Ministry of Rites ranked him first among all education intendants.

sentences.zh: 六年卒於官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the sixth year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 誌堅少與李流芳同學，為詩文，法唐、宋名家。

translations.literal: Zhijian in youth studied with Li Liufang; in composing poetry and prose he modeled himself on famous masters of the Tang and Song.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijian studied in youth with Li Liufang and modeled his poetry and prose on the great masters of the Tang and Song.

sentences.zh: 通籍後，卜居吳門古南園，杜門卻掃，肆誌讀書，先經後史，先史後子、集。

translations.literal: After entering the official registers he chose to live at the Old South Garden in Wu Gate, shut his doors and swept away visitors, and devoted himself wholeheartedly to reading—first the classics, then histories; first histories, then masters and collected writings.
translations.idiomatic: After entering official life he settled at the Old South Garden in Suzhou, shut his doors to visitors, and devoted himself to reading—classics first, then histories; histories first, then masters and collected writings.

sentences.zh: 其讀經，先箋疏而後辨論。

translations.literal: In reading the classics, he began with commentaries and glosses and only afterward moved to disputation.
translations.idiomatic: In reading the classics he began with commentaries and glosses before turning to disputation.

sentences.zh: 讀史，先證據而後發明。

translations.literal: In reading history, he began with evidence and only afterward moved to exposition.
translations.idiomatic: In reading history he began with evidence before moving to interpretation.

sentences.zh: 讀子，則謂唐、宋而後無子，當取說家之有裨經史者補之。

translations.literal: In reading masters, he held that after the Tang and Song there were no true masters, and that one should supplement them with commentators whose work benefited the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: In reading masters he held that after the Tang and Song there were no true philosophical masters, and that one should supplement them with commentators whose work illuminated the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 讀集，則定秦、漢以後古文為五編，考核唐、宋碑誌，援史傳，捃雜說，以參核其事之同異、文之純駁。

translations.literal: In reading collected writings, he fixed post-Qin and Han ancient prose into five compilations; he examined Tang and Song stele inscriptions and epitaphs, drew on historical biographies, and gathered miscellaneous accounts to cross-check the sameness and difference of events and the purity and impurity of texts.
translations.idiomatic: In reading collected writings he organized post-Qin and Han ancient prose into five compilations, examined Tang and Song stele inscriptions and epitaphs, drew on historical biographies and gathered miscellaneous accounts to compare events and assess the reliability of texts.

sentences.zh: 其於內典，亦深辨性相之宗。

translations.literal: Regarding Buddhist scriptures too, he deeply distinguished the schools of nature and appearance.
translations.idiomatic: In Buddhist scriptures as well he made deep distinctions among the schools of nature and appearance.

sentences.zh: 作詩甚富，自選止七十余首。

translations.literal: The poetry he wrote was very abundant; from it he selected only a little more than seventy pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a great deal of poetry but selected only some seventy pieces for preservation.

sentences.zh: 弟誌長，字平仲，舉於鄉，亦深於經學。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhichang, courtesy name Pingzhong, passed the provincial examination and was also deeply versed in classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhichang, courtesy name Pingzhong, passed the provincial examination and was also deeply versed in classical learning.

sentences.zh: 艾南英，字千子，東鄉人。

translations.literal: Ai Nanying, courtesy name Qianzi, was a native of Dongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Ai Nanying, courtesy name Qianzi, was from Dongxiang.

sentences.zh: 七歲作《竹林七賢論》。

translations.literal: At seven he wrote the 《Essay on the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove》.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he wrote the 《Essay on the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove》.

sentences.zh: 長為諸生，好學無所不窺。

translations.literal: When grown he became a licentiate; he loved learning and left nothing unexplored.
translations.idiomatic: As an adult he became a licentiate; he loved learning and explored every field.

sentences.zh: 萬歷末，場屋文腐爛，南英深疾之，與同郡章世純、羅萬藻、陳際泰以興起斯文為任，乃刻四人所作行之世。

translations.literal: Near the end of Wanli, examination essays had grown rotten; Nanying deeply deplored this, and together with his fellow prefectural graduates Zhang Shichun, Luo Wanzao, and Chen Jitai took upon themselves the task of reviving refined letters; they had the four men's writings carved and circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Wanli reign, examination essays had grown stale and formulaic; Nanying deplored this deeply, and together with his fellow graduates Zhang Shichun, Luo Wanzao, and Chen Jitai took it upon themselves to revive serious letters; they published the four men's writings.

sentences.zh: 世人翕然歸之，稱為章、羅、陳、艾。

translations.literal: People of the age flocked to them as one and called them Zhang, Luo, Chen, and Ai.
translations.idiomatic: The literary world flocked to them, calling them Zhang, Luo, Chen, and Ai.

sentences.zh: 天啟四年，南英始舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianqi Nanying first passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Nanying first passed the provincial examination in the fourth year of Tianqi.

sentences.zh: 座主檢討丁乾學、給事中郝土膏發策詆魏忠賢，南英對策亦有譏刺語。

translations.literal: His chief examiner, the reviser Ding Ganxue, and the supervising censor Hao Tugao set examination questions denouncing Wei Zhongxian; Nanying's examination answers also contained words of mockery.
translations.idiomatic: His chief examiner, the reviser Ding Ganxue, and the supervising censor Hao Tugao set examination questions denouncing Wei Zhongxian, and Nanying's answers also contained satirical remarks.

sentences.zh: 忠賢怒，削考官籍，南英亦停三科。

translations.literal: Zhongxian was angry; the examiners were struck from the registers, and Nanying was barred from three examination cycles.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian was furious; the examiners were struck from the rolls, and Nanying was barred from the examinations for three cycles.

sentences.zh: 章世純，字大力，臨川人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shichun, courtesy name Dali, was a native of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shichun, courtesy name Dali, was from Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 博聞強記。

translations.literal: Broadly informed and with a powerful memory.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly learned with an extraordinary memory.

sentences.zh: 舉天啟元年鄉試。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination in the first year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the first year of the Tianqi reign.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，累官柳州知府，年已七十矣，聞京師變，悲憤，遘疾卒。

translations.literal: During Chongzhen he rose through successive offices to prefect of Liuzhou; he was already seventy when he heard of the upheaval in the capital, grieved and indignant, fell ill, and died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign he rose to prefect of Liuzhou; he was already seventy when news of the fall of the capital reached him; grief and indignation brought on an illness, and he died.

sentences.zh: 羅萬藻，字文止，世純同縣人。

translations.literal: Luo Wanzao, courtesy name Wenzhi, was from the same county as Shichun.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Wanzao, courtesy name Wenzhi, was from the same county as Zhang Shichun.

sentences.zh: 天啟七年舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianqi he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the seventh year of Tianqi.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中行保舉法，祭酒倪元璐以萬藻應詔，辭不就。

translations.literal: During Chongzhen the recommendation system was implemented; the Chancellor of the Imperial Academy Ni Yuanlu nominated Wanzao in response to the imperial edict, but he declined and did not take up office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongzhen reign the recommendation system was implemented; Chancellor of the Imperial Academy Ni Yuanlu nominated Wanzao by imperial edict, but he declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 福王時為上杭知縣。

translations.literal: During the reign of the Prince of Fu he served as magistrate of Shanghang.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of the Prince of Fu he served as magistrate of Shanghang.

sentences.zh: 唐王立於閩，擢禮部主事。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Tang established himself in Fujian, Wanzao was promoted to secretary in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Tang established his court in Fujian, Wanzao was promoted to secretary in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 南英卒，哭而殯之，居數月亦卒。

translations.literal: When Nanying died, Wanzao wept and laid him out for burial; after several months he too died.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanying died, Wanzao mourned him and laid him out for burial; several months later he too died.

sentences.zh: 陳際泰，字大士，亦臨川人，父流寓汀州武平，生於其地。

translations.literal: Chen Jitai, courtesy name Dashi, was also from Linchuan; his father had sojourned in Wuping, Tingzhou, and he was born there.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jitai, courtesy name Dashi, was also from Linchuan; his father had settled temporarily in Wuping, Tingzhou, where Jitai was born.

sentences.zh: 家貧，不能從師，又無書，時取旁舍兒書，屏人竊誦。

translations.literal: The family was poor; he could not follow a teacher and had no books of his own; he would sometimes take a neighbor child's book, withdraw alone, and recite it in secret.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor; he could not afford a teacher and had no books of his own, so he would borrow a neighbor child's book, slip away alone, and recite it in secret.

sentences.zh: 從外兄所獲《書經》，四角已漫滅，且無句讀，自以意識別之，遂通其義。

translations.literal: From a maternal cousin he obtained a copy of the 《Book of Documents》 whose four corners were already worn away and which had no punctuation; relying on his own understanding to distinguish the phrases, he came to grasp its meaning.
translations.idiomatic: From a maternal cousin he obtained a copy of the 《Book of Documents》 whose corners were worn away and which had no punctuation; by working out the phrasing on his own he mastered its meaning.

sentences.zh: 十歲，於外家藥籠中見《詩經》，取而疾走。

translations.literal: At ten, in his maternal family's medicine chest he saw the 《Book of Songs》, took it, and ran off swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he spotted the 《Book of Songs》 in his maternal family's medicine chest, snatched it, and ran off.

sentences.zh: 父見之，怒，督往田，則攜至田所，踞高阜而哦，遂畢身不忘。

translations.literal: His father saw this, grew angry, and ordered him to the fields; he would carry the book to the field, sit atop a high mound and chant, and thus remembered it for life.
translations.idiomatic: His father caught him, grew angry, and sent him to work in the fields; Jitai would take the book along, sit on a high mound and chant, and thus memorized it for life.

sentences.zh: 久之，返臨川，與南英輩以時文名天下。

translations.literal: After a long while he returned to Linchuan; together with Nanying and the others he became famous throughout the realm for examination essays.
translations.idiomatic: After many years he returned to Linchuan and, together with Nanying and the others, became famous throughout the realm for examination essays.

sentences.zh: 其為文，敏甚，一日可二三十首，先後所作至萬首，經生舉業之富，無若際泰者。

translations.literal: In composing essays he was extremely quick; in a single day he could produce twenty or thirty pieces, and his writings over time reached ten thousand—among licentiates in examination composition, none was as prolific as Jitai.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote with extraordinary speed, producing twenty or thirty essays in a single day; his total output eventually reached ten thousand pieces—no licentiate in examination composition was as prolific as Jitai.

sentences.zh: 崇禎三年舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chongzhen he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chongzhen he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 又四年成進士，年六十有八矣。

translations.literal: Four years later he passed the jinshi examination, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later he earned his jinshi degree, at the age of sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 又三年除行人。

translations.literal: Three years later he was appointed Courier.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he was appointed a courier.

sentences.zh: 居四年，護故相蔡國用喪南行，卒於道。

translations.literal: After four years in office, he escorted the funeral of the former chief minister Cai Guoyong southward and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: After four years in office, he escorted the funeral of the former chief minister Cai Guoyong southward and died on the journey.

sentences.zh: 張溥，字天如，太倉人。

translations.literal: Zhang Pu, whose courtesy name was Tianru, was a native of Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pu, styled Tianru, came from Taicang.

sentences.zh: 伯父輔之，南京工部尚書。

translations.literal: His uncle Fuzhi served as Minister of Works at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Fuzhi served as minister of works at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 溥幼嗜學。

translations.literal: Pu from youth loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Pu loved learning.

sentences.zh: 所讀書必手鈔，鈔已朗誦一過，即焚之，又鈔，如是者六七始已。

translations.literal: Every book he read he copied by hand; once copied he would recite it aloud once, then burn it and copy again—six or seven times before he was done.
translations.idiomatic: Every book he read he copied by hand; once copied he would recite it aloud once, then burn it and copy again—six or seven times before he was satisfied.

sentences.zh: 右手握管處，指掌成繭。

translations.literal: Where his right hand held the brush, fingers and palm formed calluses.
translations.idiomatic: Where his right hand held the brush, his fingers and palm were covered with calluses.

sentences.zh: 冬日手皸，日沃湯數次。

translations.literal: In winter his hands cracked; he poured hot water over them several times a day.
translations.idiomatic: In winter his hands cracked, and he poured hot water over them several times a day.

sentences.zh: 後名讀書之齋曰「七錄」，以此也。

translations.literal: Later he named his study 「Seven Recordings」, for this reason.
translations.idiomatic: Later he named his study "Seven Recordings" for this reason.

sentences.zh: 與同里張采共學齊名，號「婁東二張」。

translations.literal: He studied together with his fellow townsman Zhang Cai and shared equal fame, being called 「The Two Zhangs of Loudong.」
translations.idiomatic: He studied together with his fellow townsman Zhang Cai and shared equal fame, being called "The Two Zhangs of Loudong."

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年以選貢生入都，采方成進士，兩人名徹都下。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he entered the capital as a selected tribute student; Cai had just passed the jinshi, and both men's names resounded throughout the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen he entered the capital as a selected tribute student; Cai had just earned his jinshi degree, and both men's names resounded throughout the capital.

sentences.zh: 已而采官臨川。

translations.literal: Before long Cai took office in Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Cai took office in Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 溥歸，集郡中名士相與復古學，名其文社日復社。

translations.literal: Pu returned home, gathered eminent scholars of the prefecture to revive ancient learning together, and named their literary society the Restoration Society.
translations.idiomatic: Pu returned home, gathered eminent scholars of the prefecture to revive ancient learning together, and named their literary society the Fushe Restoration Society.

sentences.zh: 四年成進士，改庶吉士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he passed the jinshi and was transferred to Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he earned his jinshi degree and was made a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 以葬親乞假歸，讀者若經生，無間寒暑。

translations.literal: He requested leave to return home to bury his parents and read like a classicist, without interruption summer or winter.
translations.idiomatic: He requested leave to return home to bury his parents and read like a classicist, without pause through summer and winter.

sentences.zh: 四方啖名者爭走其門，盡名為復社。

translations.literal: Those hungry for fame from the four quarters rushed to his door; all were named members of the Restoration Society.
translations.idiomatic: Those hungry for fame from every quarter rushed to his door; all were enrolled as members of the Restoration Society.

sentences.zh: 溥亦傾身結納，交遊日廣，聲氣通朝右。

translations.literal: Pu also devoted himself to forming alliances; his associations grew daily, and his influence reached the highest officials at court.
translations.idiomatic: Pu also devoted himself to forming alliances; his associations grew daily, and his influence reached the highest officials at court.

sentences.zh: 所品題甲乙，頗能為榮辱。

translations.literal: The rankings he assigned could greatly bring honor or disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: The rankings he assigned could greatly bring honor or disgrace.

sentences.zh: 諸奔走附麗者，輒自矜曰：「吾以嗣東林也。」

translations.literal: Those who rushed to attach themselves would boast: 「We are the successors of the Donglin faction.
translations.idiomatic: Those who rushed to attach themselves would boast: "We are the successors of the Donglin faction.

sentences.zh: 執政大僚由此惡之。

translations.literal: The great officials in power therefore hated them.
translations.idiomatic: The great officials in power therefore hated them.

sentences.zh: 裏人陸文聲者，輸貲為監生，求入社不許，采又嘗以事抶之。

translations.literal: A fellow townsman, Lu Wensheng, paid money to become a student of the Imperial Academy and sought to join the society but was refused; Cai had also once beaten him over an affair.
translations.idiomatic: A fellow townsman, Lu Wensheng, paid money to become a student of the Imperial Academy and sought to join the society but was refused; Cai had also once beaten him over an affair.

sentences.zh: 文聲詣闕言：「風俗之弊，皆原於士子。

translations.literal: Wensheng went to the palace gate and said: 「The corruption of customs all originates with the literati.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng went to the palace gate and said: "The corruption of customs all originates with the literati.

sentences.zh: 溥、采為主盟，倡復社，亂天下。」

translations.literal: Pu and Cai lead the alliance, advocate the Restoration Society, and throw the realm into disorder.」
translations.idiomatic: Pu and Cai lead the alliance, advocate the Restoration Society, and throw the realm into disorder.

sentences.zh: 溫體仁方枋國事，下所司。

translations.literal: Wen Tiren was then directing state affairs and sent the matter down to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tiren was then directing state affairs and sent the matter down to the responsible offices.

sentences.zh: 遷延久之，提學御史倪元珙、兵備參議馮元揚、太倉知州周仲連言復社無可罪。

translations.literal: After long delay, Education Censor Ni Yuangong, Defense Assistant Administrator Feng Yuanyang, and Taicang Prefect Zhou Zhonglian said the Restoration Society was guilty of nothing.
translations.idiomatic: After a long delay, Education Censor Ni Yuangong, Defense Assistant Administrator Feng Yuanyang, and Taicang Prefect Zhou Zhonglian said the Restoration Society was guilty of nothing.

sentences.zh: 三人皆貶斥，嚴旨窮究不已。

translations.literal: All three were demoted and dismissed; stern edicts demanded investigation without end.
translations.idiomatic: All three were demoted and dismissed; stern edicts demanded investigation without end.

sentences.zh: 閩人周之夔者，嘗為蘇州推官，坐事罷去，疑溥為之，恨甚。

translations.literal: Zhou Zhikui of Fujian had once served as judicial assistant in Suzhou; dismissed for an offense, he suspected Pu was behind it and hated him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zhikui of Fujian had once served as judicial assistant in Suzhou; dismissed for an offense, he suspected Pu was behind it and hated him deeply.

sentences.zh: 聞文聲訐溥，遂伏闕言溥等把持計典，己罷職實其所為，因及復社恣橫狀。

translations.literal: Hearing Wensheng's accusation against Pu, he prostrated himself at the palace gate and said Pu and others controlled the examination system, that his dismissal was actually their doing, and described the overbearing conduct of the Restoration Society.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Wensheng's accusation against Pu, he prostrated himself at the palace gate and said Pu and others controlled the examination system, that his dismissal was actually their doing, and described the overbearing conduct of the Restoration Society.

sentences.zh: 章下，巡撫張國維等言之夔去官，無預溥事，亦被旨譙讓。

translations.literal: When the memorial was sent down, Grand Coordinator Zhang Guowei and others said Zhikui's dismissal had nothing to do with Pu, but they too received an edict of rebuke.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was sent down, Grand Coordinator Zhang Guowei and others said Zhikui's dismissal had nothing to do with Pu, but they too received an edict of rebuke.

sentences.zh: 至十四年，溥已卒，而事猶未竟。

translations.literal: By the fourteenth year Pu had already died, yet the affair was still unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: By the fourteenth year Pu had already died, yet the affair was still unresolved.

sentences.zh: 刑部侍郎蔡奕琛坐黨薛國觀系獄，未知溥卒也，訐溥遙握朝柄，己罪由溥，因言采結黨亂政。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Justice Cai Yichen, imprisoned for association with Xue Guoguan, not knowing Pu was dead, accused Pu of wielding court power from afar, said his own crime was Pu's doing, and charged Cai with factionalism and disordering government.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Justice Cai Yichen, imprisoned for association with Xue Guoguan, not knowing Pu was dead, accused Pu of wielding court power from afar, said his own crime was Pu's doing, and charged Zhang Cai with factionalism and disordering government.

sentences.zh: 詔責溥、采回奏，采上言：「復社非臣事，然臣與溥生平相淬礪，死避網羅，負義圖全，誼不出此。
