translations.literal: An edict demanded that Pu and Cai respond; Cai memorialized: 「The Restoration Society is not my affair, yet Pu and I tempered each other throughout our lives; now dead he cannot escape the net, and to save myself by betraying righteousness—friendship does not permit this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict demanded that Pu and Cai respond; Cai memorialized: "The Restoration Society is not my affair, yet Pu and I tempered each other throughout our lives; now dead he cannot escape the net, and to save myself by betraying righteousness—friendship does not permit this.

sentences.zh: 念溥日夜解經論文，矢心報稱，曾未一日服官，懷忠入地。

translations.literal: Consider that Pu day and night expounded the classics and wrote essays, vowed his heart to repay the realm, never served a single day in office, and took his loyalty to the grave.
translations.idiomatic: Consider that Pu day and night expounded the classics and wrote essays, vowed his heart to repay the realm, never served a single day in office, and took his loyalty to the grave.

sentences.zh: 即今嚴綸之下，並不得泣血自明，良足哀悼。」

translations.literal: Even now under stern edicts he cannot weep blood to clear himself—this is truly worthy of mourning.」
translations.idiomatic: Even now under stern edicts he cannot weep blood to clear himself—this is truly worthy of mourning.

sentences.zh: 當是時，體仁已前罷，繼者張至發、薛國觀皆不喜東林，故所司不敢復奏。

translations.literal: At that time Tiren had already been dismissed earlier; his successors Zhang Zhifa and Xue Guoguan both disliked the Donglin faction, so the responsible offices dared not memorialize again.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Tiren had already been dismissed earlier; his successors Zhang Zhifa and Xue Guoguan both disliked the Donglin faction, so the responsible offices dared not memorialize again.

sentences.zh: 及是，至發、國觀亦相繼罷，而周延儒當國，溥座主也，其獲再相，溥有力焉，故采疏上，事即得解。

translations.literal: By then Zhifa and Guoguan had also been dismissed in turn; Zhou Yanru held power—Pu had been his examination patron, and Pu had helped him regain the chancellorship—so when Cai's memorial went up, the affair was immediately resolved.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhifa and Guoguan had also been dismissed in turn; Zhou Yanru held power—Pu had been his examination patron, and Pu had helped him regain the chancellorship—so when Cai's memorial went up, the affair was immediately resolved.

sentences.zh: 明年，御史劉熙祚、給事中姜埰交章言溥砥行博聞，所纂述經史，有功聖學，宜取備乙夜觀。

translations.literal: The next year Censor Liu Xizuo and Censor-in-Chief Jiang Kan jointly memorialized that Pu's upright conduct and broad learning, and his compilations of the classics and histories, had served sagely learning and should be collected for late-night imperial reading.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Censor Liu Xizuo and Censor-in-Chief Jiang Kan jointly memorialized that Pu's upright conduct and broad learning, and his compilations of the classics and histories, had served sagely learning and should be collected for the emperor's late-night reading.

sentences.zh: 帝御經筵，問及二人，延儒對曰：「讀書好秀才。」

translations.literal: At the Classics Lecture the emperor asked about the two men; Yanru replied: 「They are good scholars who love reading.
translations.idiomatic: At the Classics Lecture the emperor asked about the two men; Yanru replied: "They are good scholars who love reading.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「溥已卒，采小臣，言官何為薦之？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 「Pu is already dead, and Cai is a minor official—why do the remonstrance officials recommend them?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Pu is already dead, and Cai is a minor official—why do the remonstrance officials recommend them?

sentences.zh: 延儒曰：「二人好讀書，能文章，言官為舉子時讀其文，又以其用未竟，故惜之耳。」

translations.literal: Yanru said: 「Both men love reading and can write well; the remonstrance officials read their writings when they were examination candidates, and because their talents were not fully used, they regret it—that is all.」
translations.idiomatic: Yanru said: "Both men love reading and can write well; the remonstrance officials read their writings when they were examination candidates, and because their talents were not fully used, they regret it—that is all."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「亦未免偏。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: 「That is still somewhat partial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "That is still somewhat partial.

sentences.zh: 延儒言：「誠如聖諭，溥與黃道周皆偏，因善讀書，以故惜之者眾。」

translations.literal: Yanru said: 「Truly as Your Majesty says, both Pu and Huang Daozhou are partial—but because they read well, many regret them.」
translations.idiomatic: Yanru said: "Truly as Your Majesty says, both Pu and Huang Daozhou are partial—but because they read well, many regret them."

sentences.zh: 帝頷之，遂有詔征溥遺書，而道周亦復官。

translations.literal: The emperor nodded, and thereupon an edict summoned Pu's surviving writings, and Daozhou was also restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded, and thereupon an edict summoned Pu's surviving writings, and Daozhou was also restored to office.

sentences.zh: 有司先後錄上三千余卷，帝悉留覽。

translations.literal: The offices recorded and submitted more than three thousand scrolls in succession; the emperor kept them all for reading.
translations.idiomatic: The offices recorded and submitted more than three thousand scrolls in succession; the emperor kept them all for reading.

sentences.zh: 溥詩文敏捷。

translations.literal: Pu's poetry and prose were swift.
translations.idiomatic: Pu's poetry and prose were swift.

sentences.zh: 四方征索者，不起草，對客揮毫，俄頃立就，以故名高一時。

translations.literal: Those who sought his work from the four quarters—he made no draft; facing guests he wielded the brush and finished in a moment, and for this his fame stood highest of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Those who sought his work from every quarter—he made no draft; facing guests he wielded the brush and finished in a moment, and for this his fame stood highest of the age.

sentences.zh: 卒時，年止四十。

translations.literal: When he died he was only forty.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was only forty.

sentences.zh: 采，字受先，與溥善。

translations.literal: Cai, whose courtesy name was Shouxian, was on good terms with Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Cai, styled Shouxian, was on good terms with Pu.

sentences.zh: 溥性寬，泛交博愛。

translations.literal: Pu's nature was broad; he made friends widely and loved many.
translations.idiomatic: Pu's nature was broad; he made friends widely and loved many.

sentences.zh: 采特嚴毅，喜甄別可否，人有過，嘗面叱之。

translations.literal: Cai was especially stern and resolute; he liked to distinguish right from wrong, and when someone erred he would rebuke him to his face.
translations.idiomatic: Cai was especially stern and resolute; he liked to distinguish right from wrong, and when someone erred he would rebuke him to his face.

sentences.zh: 知臨川，摧強扶弱，聲大起。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Linchuan he crushed the strong and supported the weak; his reputation greatly rose.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Linchuan he crushed the strong and supported the weak; his reputation greatly rose.

sentences.zh: 移疾歸，士民泣送載道。

translations.literal: He resigned on grounds of illness and returned home; officials and people wept and escorted him, filling the roads.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on grounds of illness and returned home; officials and people wept and escorted him, filling the roads.

sentences.zh: 知州劉士鬥、錢肅樂嚴重之，以奸蠹詢采，片紙報，鹹置之法。

translations.literal: Prefects Liu Shidou and Qian Sule held him in high esteem; they consulted Cai about corrupt villains, and on a single sheet of paper he would report—all were punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects Liu Shidou and Qian Sule held him in high esteem; they consulted Cai about corrupt villains, and on a single sheet of paper he would report—all were punished by law.

sentences.zh: 福王時，起禮部主事，進員外郎，乞假去。

translations.literal: During the reign of the Prince of Fu he was recalled as Secretary in the Ministry of Rites, promoted to Vice Director, then requested leave and departed.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of the Prince of Fu he was recalled as secretary in the Ministry of Rites, promoted to vice director, then requested leave and departed.

sentences.zh: 南都失守，奸人素銜采者，群擊之死，復用大錐亂刺之。

translations.literal: When the Southern Capital fell, villains who had long resented Cai attacked him in a mob and killed him, then stabbed him repeatedly with large awls.
translations.idiomatic: When the Southern Capital fell, villains who had long resented Cai attacked him in a mob and killed him, then stabbed him repeatedly with large awls.

sentences.zh: 已而蘇，避之鄰邑，又三年卒。

translations.literal: Later he revived, fled to a neighboring district, and died three years after.
translations.idiomatic: Later he revived, fled to a neighboring district, and died three years later.
